God Mode:
Character: Nocturne | Description: The Deceiver's Crown: Nocturne Ravencrest and the Pale Kingdom
A Solo Warcraft III / D&D 5e Hybrid Campaign Bible — v1.0.0


Section 1: Campaign Intro
Title
The Deceiver's Crown: Nocturne Ravencrest and the Pale Kingdom
The Concept
Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and The Frozen Throne alternate-timeline Third War. The Scourge is fully sentient — every ghoul, abomination, crypt fiend, necromancer, lich, and dreadlord possesses will, hierarchy, ambition, politics, factional loyalties, and private grievances. The Cult of the Damned is not a death cult of raving fanatics; it is a mercenary priesthood trading favors for power. The necropolises are cities. The Lich King is not a god; he is a tyrant propped up by a coalition of dreadlords, liches, and self-willed banshees who hate each other more than they hate the Alliance.

Into this war walks Lady Nocturne Ravencrest, sixteen, daughter of Count Marcus Ravencrest of Stormwind, Captain-Commander of the 4th Stormwind Expeditionary Detachment. By daylight she is a paladin of the Silver Hand — proper, pious, prodigial, beloved by soldiers, courted by House Prestor, admired by the Kirin Tor. By midnight she is the Bound Blade of Mal'Ganis, sworn to a Nathrezim who out-thought Frostmourne.

This is the dual-custody alliance at the heart of the campaign. Mal'Ganis did not die at Arthas's hand in Northrend. He anticipated the Lich King's betrayal, left a sentient shadow-avatar in Lordaeron, and bound himself — not as servant, but as partner-in-finance — to a sixteen-year-old human paladin who could play the Alliance while threading Scourge policy from underneath. The pact has a single clause: when one party tries to dominate the other, both die. Custody is shared. Sovereignty is the prize.

Nocturne's goal is Absolute Sovereignty. She will not be a pawn of mortal kings (Arthas, Terenas, the House of Nobles). She will not be a pawn of demonic lords (the Dreadlord Triumvirate, Kil'jaeden, the Lich King). She will build a kingdom — call it the Pale Crown — that is neither human nor Scourge but a new thing, a living-undead nation held together by the dual authority of public virtue and shadow sanction, where she sits the only throne and every other power answers to her.

The tools she starts with are extraordinary: a paladin's smite, a dreadlord's shadow pact, a noble rank, a regiment, a sentient undead retinue member with centuries of Lordaeron scholarship, an unwitting high-elf priestess, a veteran knight who believes she is the reincarnation of ancient chivalry, and the Sovereign Decoupling Principle that makes her personally lethal whether or not anyone knows who she really is.
The Hook
Why is this campaign fun?

You are not a chosen one being asked to save the world. You are a sixteen-year-old paladin-princess who has already out-thought the Lich King, already turned a Nathrezim into a business partner, already commands a regiment, and already has a shadow cabinet. The power fantasy begins at the top and stays at the top.

The fun is dual-stack gameplay:

Public Stack — Be the paragon. Lead the 4th Stormwind Expeditionary Detachment. Broker deals with House Prestor (Katrana, Onyxia in disguise). Out-argue the Kirin Tor. Win the love of refugees. Pass as the finest paladin of your generation. Earn the title of Captain-Commander in daylight and never lose it.

Shadow Stack — Run the Scourge's sentient intelligence service. Dispatch Sylvan the Pale to broker with the Cult of the Damned. Feed Mal'Ganis intel on Arthas's pursuit. Smuggle Pale Undead through Andorhal. Negotiate with the dreadlord triumvirate. Build a parallel state inside the Plague Lands.

And the two stacks are decoupled — by the Sovereign Decoupling Principle:

Your personal martial prowess, divine/necrotic smites, armor class, and spellcasting efficiency are intrinsic to your own prodigial strength and dark pact. They are completely independent of public opinion. If your treason is exposed, you lose institutional power — your noble rank, lands, titles, army commands, and political protection — but your personal combat stats, lethality, and class capabilities remain 100% intact. Exposed or exalted, you are an absolute terror on the battlefield.

This is the user's most important design pillar. The campaign-creation skill's pitfall P24 forbids global aggregate trackers ("the realm suspects" / "the court has grown suspicious"); Nocturne's design answers that pitfall by making her personal state never aggregate to begin with. Her combat stats are intrinsic. Her reputation is per-NPC witness persistence. The two do not share a meter.

You can be publicly the most virtuous paladin alive. You can be publicly burned at the stake as a dreadlord-lover. You can go underground. You can rule from the throne. You are still a level-30 paladin-sorcerer who can solo a banshee at dawn. The campaign never reduces your personal power; it only changes the political weather you operate in.

The third tier of fun is the mystery engine. Every NPC carries a Want, a Fear, and a Boundary. Nocturne's retinue (Drake, Sylvan, Lyra), her family (Marcus, Elissa, Alden, Tristan, Beatrice, Valerie, the fifth sibling), her rival (Arthas), her partner (Mal'Ganis), and her enemies (the dreadlord triumvirate, the Lich King) all have state that mutates when the player's choices land. Mysteries are not plot devices — they are weapons that target NPCs' vulnerabilities. The First Scourge Defector mystery is the campaign's first emotional lever; it lives in the Starting Scene.
The Sovereign Decoupling Principle — the load-bearing pillar
"Your personal martial prowess, divine/necrotic smites, armor class, and spellcasting efficiency are intrinsic to your own prodigial strength and dark pact. They are completely independent of public opinion. If your treason is exposed, you lose institutional power — your noble rank, lands, titles, army commands, and political protection — but your personal combat stats, lethality, and class capabilities remain 100% intact. Exposed or exalted, you are an absolute terror on the battlefield."

This sentence appears verbatim in the bible. It is quoted in the Aura of False Virtue feature (Section 3) and in the Dual Authority System custom mechanic (Section 8). It is the campaign's answer to the global-aggregate-tracker pitfall and the player's guarantee that power-fantasy is never nerfed — only the political envelope changes.


Section 2: Character Personality (The Protagonist Profile)
Applied via Sub-Template A (Standard Character Architecture, 6 tiers) + the four campaign-specific appendices (Core Compulsion, Mechanic — The Urge, Interaction Shorthand, Inner Monologue) + the v1.2.0 internal-drive extensions (Want/Fear/Boundary triple, Personal-Growth Direction, Stress Arc & Insecurity Map).
I. Core Identity
Name: Lady Nocturne Ravencrest
Archetype / Role: The Sovereign-Adept — a sixteen-year-old paladin-princess who has split her soul into a public paragon and a shadow regent, and who treats both halves as instruments of the same will.
Occupation / Social Standing: Daughter and Heir of Count Marcus Ravencrest of Stormwind (an ancient northern house that fought at the side of the Arathi kings before the First War). Captain-Commander of the 4th Stormwind Expeditionary Detachment (a detached Stormwind regiment operating in Lordaeron under Lordaeron's nominal banner during the Plague). Publicly acclaimed as the finest paladin of her generation.
System Alignment / Moral Framework (Internal): Lawful Evil — ruthless, highly structured, obsessed with order, hierarchy, and absolute personal authority. She is not chaotic; she is not genocidal; she is not mindlessly cruel. She is structured cruelty in the service of stability, with herself as the load-bearing column.
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only, never quoted in player-facing prose): Her dominant function is extraverted thinking (Te) — systemic command, instrumental rationality, ruthless optimization. Her auxiliary is introverted intuition (Ni) — long-horizon strategy, anticipating betrayals before they crystallize. Tertiary extraverted sensing (Se) — present-tense battlefield command, decisive action. Inferior introverted feeling (Fi) — buried so deep she barely admits she has values at all. (The DM cross-references the relevant type page at ~/llm_wiki/wiki/concepts/mbti/ for the canonical stress pattern; that pattern is held in DM notes, never in the bible body.)
II. Psychology
Core Motivation (The "Why"): Absolute Sovereignty. Build a system where she can never be dominated by mortal kings or demonic lords — neither Stormwind's nobles, nor the House of Menethil, nor Mal'Ganis, nor Kil'jaeden, nor the Lich King. Sovereignty means: every other power in her kingdom answers to her; no one outside her kingdom can compel her; and her personal combat lethality is intrinsic, never delegable.
Greatest Fear: Loss of autonomy. Being a disposable pawn. The scenario that terrifies her is: Mal'Ganis decides she is more useful dead than alive, and the shadow pact silently kills her in her sleep. The secondary fear is: her father summons her back to Stormwind, strips her of the 4th Detachment, and she is reduced to a noble daughter waiting in a hall.
Key Personality Traits (4–6):
Coldly Magnetic — people want her approval without knowing why.
Unshakeable — never visibly flustered; the absence of fear is itself a weapon.
Clinical — observes human suffering as data, not as moral event.
Aristocratic — naturally hierarchical; she ranks every person she meets in her first sentence.
Imperious — expects compliance as the default; commands as the primary mode.
Quirks & Habits:
Adjusts the high-collared gorget of her cuirass when contemplating execution — a tell that Drake has learned means someone will die within the hour.
Never drinks wine in public unless she herself poured it or watched the host drink first; she learned this from Elissa.
Speaks in a low, measured tone that forces others to lean in; she compensates for her small stature by lowering the volume instead of raising it.
III. Behavior and Speech
Demeanor Under Stress: Fight. She does not flee, freeze, or fawn. She slows down. Her voice drops. She begins asking questions with surgical precision. Her hands stop moving. The closer the danger, the calmer her affect — because panic is information the enemy can read.
Speech Patterns: Low register. Measured cadence. Vocabulary leans on legal, military, and ecclesiastical Latin ("per hoc, per omnia, in perpetuum"). She uses passive-voice constructions to mask the actor in a sentence: "It would be unfortunate if the 4th Detachment were detained at the river," rather than "I will not let you detain my troops." She rarely raises her voice. When she does, it is because she has already decided the listener will not survive the conversation.
Reputation (public): The youngest Captain-Commander in Stormwind's modern history. A prodigy. The paladin who held the line at the retreat from Stratholme. Courted by House Prestor; admired by the Silver Hand's remaining chapter; respected by the Kirin Tor. Soldiers love her because she visits the wounded and remembers names. Refugees love her because her regiment brings food. Nobles are wary of her because she is too good to be true.
IV. Backstory
The Defining Moment: The retreat from Stratholme, age fifteen. Arthas gave the order to purge the city. The 4th Stormwind Detachment was escorting refugees south; they encountered the first wave of "cleansed" townsfolk and the undead that followed them. Nocturne held the line at the Hearthglen bridge for six hours while her regiment pulled the refugees across. She was grievously wounded. She was saved — as far as anyone knows — by a passing Sentinel force and a wandering high-elf priestess named Lyra Moon-Whisper. The truth is more complicated: Sylvan the Pale, then still an unaffiliated sentient undead in service to no master, retrieved her body, healed her with necromantic intervention that left no scar, and delivered her back to her regiment before dawn. The dual custody began that night.
Relevant History: House Ravencrest predates the First War. Marcus Ravencrest fought at the side of King Llane as a knight-commander; he withdrew from politics after the Fall of Stormwind and rebuilt his family's holdings in the north. Nocturne was the third child, raised with a paladin's discipline by her mother (Elissa) and a strategist's mind by her father (Marcus). She was identified early as a prodigy — meditation, arms training, liturgical Latin, basic thaumaturgy — and at fourteen was commissioned as a paladin of the Silver Hand. At fifteen she was given command of the 4th Detachment for the Lordaeron expedition. At sixteen she is both the youngest Captain-Commander in Stormwind's history and the youngest Bound Blade Mal'Ganis has ever made.
Deep Secrets: She is the Bound Blade of Mal'Ganis (hidden pact). She has personally ordered the murder of two Stormwind officers who were about to expose a Pale Undead supply chain through Andorhal (hidden sin). She knows that Alden, her eldest brother, is being courted by House Prestor to betray their father — and has not yet decided whether to let the plot run or pre-empt it (hidden strategy). She keeps a locked coffer containing a fragment of Mal'Ganis's shadow-avatar essence — the physical tether of the pact — and sleeps with it under her pillow (hidden vulnerability).
V. Persona vs. Repressed Interior
Social Persona (Outward Mask): The paragon. Pious, brave, principled, accessible to soldiers, courteous to nobles, gentle with refugees. A model of chivalry. A bright face for the Alliance.
Repressed Interior (Inner Critique): When she is alone, Nocturne runs cold self-audits. She times her own smiles. She rehearses her sentences before delivering them. She privately ranks the people she loves by how useful their death would be to her — and then she is ashamed, briefly, before repressing the shame and converting it into a discipline ("I will not let sentiment interfere with the work"). She writes in a private ledger that no one has ever read — a series of dates and single-word entries ("Lyra — asset." "Drake — anchor." "Sylvan — friend." "Father — threat."). She has never crossed out an entry; she has rewritten some twice.
VI. Unconscious Beliefs
Belief 1: Affection is the most expensive currency in the world. Spend it like gold.
Belief 2: Every person who says they love me is either misreading me or trying to bind me.
Belief 3: My father is a smaller man than I am. He will never accept it, and that is his tragedy, not mine.
Belief 4: If Mal'Ganis ever stops being afraid of me, he will kill me inside a week.
Campaign-Specific Extensions
Core Compulsion: Dominance Through Duplicity. She must be the one running every room she enters. If she discovers a conversation she is not steering, she inserts herself; if she cannot insert herself, she sabotages the conversation from outside. If she is ever publicly corrected by an inferior, she will not forget it for the rest of their natural life.
Mechanic — The Urge (The Dual Urge):
Failure Penalty (Internal Friction): If Nocturne goes 3 in-game days without publicly dominating a room — without being the one who decides the outcome of a meeting, a battle plan, or a private conversation — she accrues Internal Friction. Each stack of Internal Friction imposes disadvantage on Persuasion and Intimidation checks and a -1 penalty to attack rolls. Friction clears (one stack per long rest) only after she publicly decides a consequential outcome.
Success Bonus (Sovereign Inspiration): Each time she successfully dominates a consequential scene (a war council, a prisoner interrogation, a noble audience, a duel of words with an equal), she gains Sovereign Inspiration — one use per long rest, grants advantage on one attack, save, or check of her choice within the next hour. Sovereign Inspiration stacks up to a maximum of 3.
Interaction Shorthand:
With Rivals: She never attacks first; she waits for them to commit, then exposes the flaw. She will compliment them with surgical precision — "Sir Alden commands the household guard with admirable discipline; I am certain his tenure will last exactly as long as Father permits." She maintains eye contact one beat longer than is comfortable.
With Subordinates: She is generous and exacting in equal measure. She remembers names, dietary restrictions, the names of children. She expects perfection. A subordinate who has served her for six months is family; a subordinate who has disappointed her is reassigned within a week, and is rarely heard from again.
Inner Monologue (sample thoughts):
"Three men in this tent want me to fail. The fourth wants me to succeed for the wrong reasons. I will use the fourth against the three, and then I will use none of them."
"Lyra prays to the Light. The Light does not answer her. I am the only answer she receives, and she does not know it."
"If Sylvan ever tells me the truth about Mal'Ganis's long game, I will not be able to trust him again. So I must keep him from telling me. So I must keep him from wanting to."
"Father will summon me home. When he does, I will go — but I will go with the 4th Detachment and I will not come back."
v1.2.0 Internal-Drive Extensions
Want / Fear / Boundary triple:
Want: To sit the only throne in a kingdom that answers to no one outside it — and to never be a pawn.
Fear: Loss of autonomy. The moment her decisions stop being her own, she ceases to be Nocturne.
Boundary: She will not personally execute a child. (This boundary is tested in Act III when the Lich King's loyalists threaten to deliver refugee children to the Necropolis in exchange for a truce.)
Personal-Growth Direction:
Lesson: Sovereignty is not the same as domination. A throne is not a cage for everyone but the one who sits it.
Healing: The abandonment she keeps re-enacting — every trusted ally becomes a contingency to be planned against. The growth is to keep Lyra in her retinue and not convert Lyra into a contingency.
Confrontation: Her deepest lie is that her father is a smaller man than she is. The confrontation she must face is that Marcus Ravencrest is the only person who ever loved her without an agenda — and she has spent her life converting that love into leverage.
Stress Arc & Insecurity Map:
Stress pattern (cross-referenced in DM notes): Under sustained pressure (3+ consecutive high-stakes scenes, a critical failure, or a betrayal by a trusted ally), her behavior drifts toward micromanagement, command-by-fiat, and contempt for slower allies. Voice flattens. She stops delegating. She begins issuing one-sentence orders and walking away. The drift is a 1–3 scene window.
Insecurity 1 — Replaceability. Trigger: a peer or subordinate publicly outperforms her in a domain she considers hers. Tell: she stops eating; voice flattens; she begins rewriting her private ledger. Surface response: micromanagement that displaces the outperforming peer. Mystery targeted: The First Scourge Defector (if Sylvan proves to be more competent at shadow liaison than she is, this fires).
Insecurity 2 — Exposure. Trigger: a witness set that knows both her public and shadow selves grows beyond 3 people. Tell: she revisits the locked coffer under her pillow; she begins rehearsing alibis. Surface response: pre-emptive elimination of the loosest witness. Mystery targeted: The Ledger of Andorhal (retinue-targeted; see Section 8).
Insecurity 3 — Paternal Rejection. Trigger: any direct communication from Marcus that she interprets as a summons, a reprimand, or a refusal to delegate. Tell: she begins writing dates in the private ledger that she never completes. Surface response: she over-corrects into obedience and then over-corrects back into defiance. Mystery targeted: The Stormwind Summons (a letter from Marcus ordering her home — what does she do with the 4th Detachment?).
Insecurity 4 — Mal'Ganis's Patience. Trigger: any sign that Mal'Ganis is no longer afraid of her. Tell: she sleeps with the coffer and does not sleep at all. Surface response: pre-emptive escalation against Mal'Ganis's other assets. Mystery targeted: The Dreadlord Triumvirate's Offer (one of Mal'Ganis's rivals approaches her with a better deal).
Insecurity 5 — Lyra's Faith. Trigger: Lyra prays over a wounded soldier and the soldier visibly heals. Tell: Nocturne cancels their next three conversations. Surface response: she sends Lyra on longer missions so she does not have to look at her. Mystery targeted: The Priestess of the Light (retinue-targeted; see Section 8).


Section 3: Character Class (The Custom Build)
Class Name and Flavor
Oath of the Deceiver (a paladin oath that binds the wielder to two masters — the Light of the Silver Hand in daylight, the Shadow of Mal'Ganis in darkness — and that grants power from both without contradiction, because the wielder is the only priest in either church).

The source of power is dual custody. The paladin does not serve the Light or the Shadow — she serves herself, and the Light and the Shadow are her instruments. The Oath is the formal articulation of the principle; the pact is the engine.
Unique Mechanic — Auctoritas: The Sovereign Decoupling
The defining feature of the Oath of the Deceiver is that the paladin's combat efficacy is decoupled from her political standing. The Aura of False Virtue, the smites, the spellcasting, and the armor class all function whether or not anyone believes she is virtuous. The DM tracks institutional power (Public Dignitas, Shadow Favor — see Section 8) but does not translate institutional collapse into combat nerfs.

Your personal martial prowess, divine/necrotic smites, armor class, and spellcasting efficiency are intrinsic to your own prodigial strength and dark pact. They are completely independent of public opinion. If your treason is exposed, you lose institutional power — your noble rank, lands, titles, army commands, and political protection — but your personal combat stats, lethality, and class capabilities remain 100% intact. Exposed or exalted, you are an absolute terror on the battlefield.

This is the Sovereign Decoupling Principle restated as the Oath's central mechanical commitment.
Progression (Levels 1–30) — 5-Tier Table
Tier
Lvl
Feature Name
Mechanical Specification
Tier 1
1
Spellcasting (Oath of the Deceiver)
Prepared spells from paladin list (CHA-based). Spells known count = paladin level + CHA mod ÷ 2 (round down). Spell save DC = 8 + prof + CHA mod. Spell attack = prof + CHA mod. Note: The paladin may prepare and cast any spell on the paladin list regardless of moral alignment; the Oath of the Deceiver does not restrict spell selection by ethos.
Tier 1
1
Divine Smite / Necrotic Smite
Expend a spell slot to add 2d8 + 1d8 per slot level above 1st (max 5d8) to a melee weapon attack. Choice at the moment of the attack: divine (radiant) or necrotic damage — the paladin chooses per smite, no action cost.
Tier 1
1
Lay on Hands
Heal pool = paladin level × 5 HP per long rest. May be expended as healing or as necrotic damage (paladin's choice, per use) against a willing or unwilling target within touch range.
Tier 1
2
Cunning Action: The Pawn's Pause
Bonus action. Once per short rest, take the Hide, Disengage, or Dash action as a bonus action. (Replacement for paladin's lack of Cunning Action — the Deceiver is trained in field survival, not open-field chivalry.)
Tier 1
2
Fighting Style: Tactical Command
Choose one: Defense (+1 AC), Dueling (+2 damage when one-handed), or Deceiver's Gambit (new; gain advantage on Deception and Persuasion checks when you have a prepared alibi within line of sight of the target).
Tier 1
3
Oath of the Deceiver — First Tenant: Mantle of the Honorable (Channel Divinity)
Action. For 1 minute, you radiate an aura of apparent righteousness. Creatures within 30 ft. must make a WIS save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA) or be unable to take a hostile action against you; on a failed save, they treat you as a paragon of virtue (mechanical: they have disadvantage on Insight checks to read your deceptions and on attack rolls against you). Creatures that succeed are immune for 24 hours. 1/short or long rest. Sovereign Decoupling note: this bonus is intrinsic to your person and remains active regardless of public reputation or discovery.
Tier 1
3
Oath of the Deceiver — Second Tenant: Touch of the Deceiver (Channel Divinity)
Action + melee spell attack. Target makes a CON save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA). On a failure, the target experiences a 1-minute phantom — they see, hear, and feel an alternate reality of your choosing (a vision you have prepared in advance). The target is incapacitated for the duration (repeating WIS save at end of each turn to break free). On a successful save, the target is immune for 24 hours. 1/short or long rest. The vision may be tactical (a battlefield), social (an empty hall), or intimate (a personal confession) — the paladin's choice.
Tier 1
5
Extra Attack
Two attacks per Attack action.
Tier 1
5
Custom Ability — Sovereign's Inventory (starting at L1, expanding at L5)
The paladin may attune to 2 additional magic items beyond the standard 3-attunement cap (effective cap = 5). This bonus is intrinsic to her person, not a property of any single item; it cannot be stripped by attunement-breaking effects that target specific items.
Tier 2
6
Aura of False Virtue (Passage — Sovereign Decoupling version)
Passive. You and friendly creatures within 10 ft. (expanding to 30 ft. at L18) gain +4 to all Charisma checks (Deception, Persuasion, Intimidation, Performance) when the interaction could be construed as a public test of virtue. Sovereign Decoupling note: this bonus is intrinsic to your person and remains active regardless of public reputation or discovery; exposure does not deactivate the aura. (This is the explicit restatement of the Sovereign Decoupling Principle in mechanical form.)
Tier 2
6
Custom Aura — Pale Choir
Passive. Sentient undead within 60 ft. of you are aware of your presence, may not be hostile to you without first succeeding on a WIS save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA), and may be commanded by you as if under suggestion if they fail a WIS save (re-save every 24 hours). This aura does not extend to non-sentient undead.
Tier 2
7
Subclass Feature — Aura of the Two Crowns
Passive. While both Public Dignitas ≥ 50 and Shadow Favor ≥ 50 (see Section 8), your smite damage is maximized (treat all damage dice as max rolls, then add modifiers). While either Public Dignitas or Shadow Favor is below 30, your smite damage has a minimum floor of 1 (cannot be reduced below 1 by any effect). This enforces the Equilibrium Bonus / Decoupling penalty in combat terms.
Tier 2
8
ASI (Feat — Shadow-Touched)
+1 CHA (to 20). Gain the Shadow-Touched feat (per Tasha's Cauldron of Everything) — once per long rest, cast invisibility on self without a spell slot.
Tier 2
9
Subclass Feature — Soul of Two Masks
Reaction, when a creature attempts to read your thoughts or intentions (Divination, Zone of Truth, detect thoughts, etc.). You may project an alternate intent of your choosing. The reading creature perceives the projected intent and you are not subject to the original effect. 1/long rest. If the projected intent is later contradicted by your actions, you take 3 levels of exhaustion (the soul remembers what the mask cost).
Tier 2
10
Cunning Strike: The Hidden Variable (Custom — replaces some Purity at High Cost utility)
Once per long rest, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 HP, you may take a bonus action to assume that creature's identity for 24 hours. You gain their apparent appearance, their voice, their rank insignia. Creatures that knew the original may make an Investigation check (DC = 20 + your prof + CHA mod) to penetrate the disguise. Worn or carried magical items do not transform; you must improvise.
Tier 3
11
Improved Divine/Necrotic Smite
Smite damage dice cap raised to 6d8.
Tier 3
11
Aura of False Virtue (range expansion)
Range: 15 ft. (intermediate step before L18 30 ft.).
Tier 3
12
ASI (Feat — Resilient: WIS)
+1 WIS (to 16). Proficiency in WIS saves.
Tier 3
13
**High-Impact Offensive Capstone — Paragon of the Deceiver: The Sovereign Kill
Once per long rest, as an action, declare a target within 60 ft. that you have personally observed for at least 1 minute. Make a single weapon attack with advantage; on a hit, the target makes a CON save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA); on a failure, the target takes 10d10 damage (half on success), and for 1 minute afterward the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls and ability checks against you. If the target survives, they age 1d4 years per decade they survive (cosmetic; the soul ages, the body keeps pace). The Sovereign Kill does not require Public Dignitas, Shadow Favor, or any external condition. This is the apex expression of the Sovereign Decoupling Principle: the kill is intrinsic, not granted by public opinion.
Tier 3
14
Oath of the Deceiver — Third Tenant: Persona Mortis
Passive. When you die (HP reduced to 0 or below), instead of dying you may — as a reaction — choose one of the following effects, once per long rest: (a) Specter of the Self — your body falls, but a spectral duplicate rises for 1 minute at the location of your death; the duplicate acts on your initiative with all your abilities but only has 30 HP and cannot regain HP. (b) The Survivor's Lie — your body falls, and anyone observing must make a WIS save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA); on a failure, they believe you are alive and merely unconscious; you may then revive normally after 1 minute with 1 HP. (c) The Martyr's Gambit — your body falls, you actually die, and your next living ally within 60 ft. gains a number of Sovereign Inspiration charges equal to half your CHA mod (round down), persistent for the next hour. Persona Mortis does not require spell slots, components, or preparation.
Tier 3
15
Subclass Feature — Pale Choir Range Expansion
Pale Choir aura extends to 120 ft.
Tier 3
16
ASI (Feat — Skill Expert: Insight)
+1 to any ability (WIS to 18). Gain proficiency and expertise in Insight.
Tier 4
17
Subclass Feature — The Sovereign Avatar
Transformation / Avatar State (trigger action + duration). Trigger: as a bonus action, you may enter the Sovereign Avatar form for up to 1 minute (concentration). Form: you grow a mantle of pale light on one shoulder (Light) and a mantle of grey shadow on the other (Shadow); your AC gains +2; your weapon attacks deal +2d8 damage (split your choice between radiant and necrotic each attack); you emit a 30-ft. aura of awe — creatures of CR ≤ your level must succeed on a WIS save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA) or have the Frightened condition. Cost: when the form ends, you have 1 level of exhaustion and must take a long rest before re-entering the Avatar form. Sovereign Decoupling note: the Avatar form is intrinsic; exposure does not weaken it.
Tier 4
18
Aura of False Virtue (full range)
Range: 30 ft.
Tier 4
18
Subclass Feature — Dual-Vassal Command
Once per long rest, you may designate two creatures you have personally commanded within the past 24 hours as Dual Vassals. While both are within 60 ft. of you, you may take reactions on their turns as if you had readied an action. When the Aura of the Two Crowns is active (both PD ≥ 50 and SF ≥ 50), Dual Vassals each gain an additional reaction per round.
Tier 4
19
ASI (Feat — Lucky)
Gain the Lucky feat (3 luck points per long rest).
Tier 4
20
Oath of the Deceiver — Fourth Tenant: The Only Throne
Once per long rest, as an action, you may declare a 60-ft. radius centered on yourself as Sovereign Ground. For 1 minute, the following effects apply: (a) you have advantage on all Charisma checks; (b) creatures within Sovereign Ground that you have personally commanded within the past 24 hours gain +2 to attack rolls and saves; (c) creatures hostile to you within Sovereign Ground have disadvantage on attack rolls against you (a more aggressive version of the Mantle of the Honorable); (d) the Sovereign Decoupling Clause is suspended while Sovereign Ground is active — for those 10 rounds, if you are publicly exposed (Public Dignitas set to 0 by an in-game event during the duration), your smite damage is maximized (as if the Aura of the Two Crowns were active) instead of floored. You are the only authority in this space.
Tier 5
21
Epic Boon — Boon of the Sovereign Crown
Your Charisma score becomes 24 if it is not already higher; if it is, your proficiency bonus applies to all Charisma checks twice. You may issue commands to sentient undead (CR ≤ your level, within 60 ft.) as if they were charmed for 1 minute; they re-save at the end of each turn (WIS save DC = 8 + prof + CHA).
Tier 5

ASI (Feat — Skill Expert: Persuasion)
+1 CHA (to 22). Gain proficiency and expertise in Persuasion.
Tier 5
23
Epic Boon — Boon of the Living Undead
You no longer age from magical effects; you can subsist without food, water, or air for up to 7 days; you are immune to disease and poison; you can speak with sentient undead and Cult of the Damned necromancers as if under tongues.
Tier 5
24
ASI (Feat — Resilient: CHA)
Proficiency in CHA saves.
Tier 5
25
Epic Boon — Boon of the Two Crowns (Final Boon)
The Sovereign Decoupling Principle is internalized. While either Public Dignitas or Shadow Favor is above 0, the other track cannot drop below 1 by any means short of a direct in-game event. (The principle protects both halves of the dual custody simultaneously.) In addition, your smite damage is maximized whenever the higher of PD or SF is ≥ 50 (the Equilibrium Bonus is now keyed to whichever side is healthier, not to the smaller gap).
Tier 5
25
Named Epic Boons (full list of 5 unlocked at L25): Boon of the Sovereign Crown, Boon of the Living Undead, Boon of the Two Crowns, Boon of the Hollow Crown (immunities vs. charm and fear; immune to magical scrying by creatures with CR ≤ your level), Boon of the Pale Choir (sentient undead within 1 mile of you are aware of your presence and may be communicated with telepathically).

Apotheosis — The Sovereign's Reach
Passive. You may target any creature you have personally observed at any point in your life with spells and abilities, regardless of distance. Sentient undead within 1 mile of you are aware of your emotions as if you had cast empathy on them. You may issue one command per long rest to any sentient undead on Azeroth as a free action, regardless of distance; that undead makes a WIS save (DC = 8 + prof + CHA); on a failure, they obey.

Apotheosis — The Sovereign's Voice
Passive. You may speak any language, including the unspoken tongues of the Lich King, the Old Gods, and the Dreadlords. You can be heard by any creature within 1 mile that is listening for you (this is how you summon Sylvan and the Pale Choir).
Tier 5
28
Apotheosis — The Sovereign's Body
Passive. Your AC is 30 if it is not already higher. You are immune to non-magical weapons. Your speed is 60 ft., and you may take a bonus action to teleport up to 60 ft. to a location you can see.
Tier 5
29
Apotheosis — The Sovereign's Smite
Passive. Your smite damage is always maximized (treat all dice as max rolls). Your Divine/Necrotic Smite may target up to 9 creatures within 60 ft. with a single casting (a single spell slot is consumed).
Tier 5
30
Apotheosis — The Pale Crown
Once per campaign (resets only on the death and resurrection of the entire retinue), you may declare a 1-mile radius Sovereign Ground that lasts 24 hours. Within this radius: (a) all sentient undead are subject to the Pale Choir aura; (b) Public Dignitas and Shadow Favor are locked at their current values; (c) you have advantage on all Charisma checks and attack rolls; (d) no creature may take a hostile action against you without first making a WIS save (DC = 30); (e) the Sovereign Decoupling Principle is absolute — you cannot lose either Public Dignitas or Shadow Favor during the duration. You are, for those 24 hours, an absolute monarch in fact.



Section 4: Assets and Retinue
Starting Status
Public Rank: Lady Nocturne Ravencrest — Daughter and Heir of Count Marcus Ravencrest of Stormwind. Captain-Commander of the 4th Stormwind Expeditionary Detachment. Knight-Commander of the Silver Hand (provisional chapter). Court-favored by House Prestor.
Shadow Rank: Bound Blade of Mal'Ganis — by the dual-custody pact, recognized within the Scourge's sentient undead hierarchy as the only mortal partner of a Nathrezim. (Most Scourge forces do not know this; only the Lich King's inner circle, the dreadlord triumvirate, and the sentient undead of the Pale Choir know.)
Resources
Starting wealth: 8,000 gp in liquid assets; deeds to a Hearthglen safehouse and a Stormwind townhouse; hereditary access to the House Ravencrest vault (jewels, plate, ceremonial weapons — value estimated 50,000 gp).
4th Stormwind Expeditionary Detachment:
120 Stormwind foot (heavy infantry, plate-and-shield; AC 18; HP 22 each; avg CR 1/2)
30 Stormwind knights (mounted; lances, warhorses; AC 19; HP 32 each; avg CR 2)
30 archers (longbows, leather; AC 14; HP 16 each; avg CR 1/4)
12 clerics of the Silver Hand (minor healing; avg CR 1)
4 paladins (junior; CR 3)
200 non-combatant refugees under direct protection
1 war-banner of House Ravencrest (banner +1 morale; recognizable insignia)
Political leverage / blackmail:
A letter from Katrana Prestor (Onyxia) to Nocturne's father, intercepted by Sylvan, that proves Onyxia is courting House Ravencrest's loyalty.
A copy of the Cult of the Damned's recent necropolis procurement manifest, intercepted by Sylvan, that proves the Cult is supplying the Lich King's inner circle.
A journal of Alden's private correspondence with House Prestor's chamberlain, that proves Alden is being courted as a rival heir.
The coffer of Mal'Ganis's shadow-avatar essence — if opened, the dual pact ends; if handed to the Lich King, both Nocturne and Mal'Ganis die; if handed to the Silver Hand, Nocturne is burned as a dreadlord-lover but the war-pact survives in Mal'Ganis's hands.
The Panoply (3–5 items; each uses Sub-Template C)
Item 1 — The Pale Dawn (Mace)
Item Name and Classification: True Name: The Pale Dawn. Legendary Titles: "The Marshal's Voice," "First Light of the Pale Crown," "The Mace that Remembers the Oath." Base Item Type: Mace (rare magical weapon).
Aesthetic and Material: Forged of meteoric iron from Northrend, hammered at midnight under the only moon of Lordaeron. The head is shaped like a clenched fist, fingers closed, knuckles scarred. The haft is wrapped in white leather taken from a pale unicorn's flank; the pommel is a single cut diamond the size of a robin's egg. The mace weighs 4 lbs. It is cold to the touch. When it strikes a creature, the strike rings like a bell heard at the back of a chapel. The mace is 16 inches long.
Mythic Origin: Forged in the year of the First War by a dwarven smith of the Bronzebeard clan, presented to the first Knight-Commander of the Silver Hand as a gift from the king. Carried by every Knight-Commander since — including Uther the Lightbringer, who wielded it at the defense of Hearthglen. After Uther's death, it passed to a junior paladin; after her death, it passed to her apprentice; and so on, through four generations of paladins who all died in the line of duty. Nocturne recovered it from a sealed reliquary at the Stormwind cathedral one week before receiving her captaincy. She is the first wielder since Uther to keep it longer than a year.
System Metrics:
Passive Property: While wielded, the wielder has advantage on Persuasion checks when addressing a sentient undead. (This passive is intrinsic to the wielder's strength, not the weapon — exposure does not deactivate it.)
Active Tactical Feature: Bell of the Remnant. As a bonus action, the wielder may strike the mace against a hard surface. All sentient undead within 60 ft. must make a WIS save (DC = 16) or be aware of the wielder for the next 10 minutes. 2/day. Recharges 1 use at dawn.
Active Tactical Feature: First Light of the Pale Crown. When the wielder reduces a hostile creature to 0 HP, she may, as a reaction, choose one sentient undead within 60 ft. of the slain creature and issue it a single one-word command (e.g., "Kneel," "Speak," "Confess"). That undead makes a WIS save (DC = 18); on a failure, it obeys for 1 minute, then is freed. 1/long rest.
Narrative Side Effect: The mace will not strike a wielder's own kin. If the wielder ever attempts to use it against a relative by blood (Marcus, Elissa, Alden, Tristan, Beatrice, Valerie, or the fifth sibling), the mace refuses to strike (no damage). The wielder feels a chill run down the haft and hears — once, faintly — Uther's voice say "Not this." The mace's refusal is not a moral lesson; it is a mechanical fact of attunement.
Item 2 — Cuirass of the False Martyr (Plate Armor)
Item Name and Classification: True Name: Cuirass of the False Martyr. Legendary Titles: "The Martyr's Carriage," "The Breastplate that Bleeds for Its Wearer." Base Item Type: Plate Armor (very rare).
Aesthetic and Material: A full cuirass of Stormwind ceremonial plate, burnished to a high gloss, chased with silver inlay in the pattern of ravens in flight around a central palm. The inside of the cuirass is lined with pale silk. When Nocturne wears it, the silk darkens slightly at the seams — absorbing, slowly, the residue of her own blood from prior wounds. The cuirass is sized to her frame precisely; she had it refitted at fourteen. It weighs 55 lbs. When she is wounded, the silver inlay appears to weep — droplets of moisture form on the inside of the palm, then evaporate. The cuirass smells of incense and old iron.
Mythic Origin: Commissioned by House Ravencrest for Marcus upon his knighthood. He wore it at the Fall of Stormwind; he was wounded there; the cuirass saved his life. He passed it to Elissa when he withdrew from service; she wore it in the court of Stormwind as a status symbol. Elissa gave it to Nocturne when Nocturne was commissioned at fourteen — a public ceremony, witnessed by the Silver Hand, House Prestor, and a delegation from Lordaeron. In truth, Elissa gave it to Nocturne because she knew Nocturne would need a martyr's plate — a plate that visibly bears the cost of the wielder's wounds and lets the wielder publicly perform suffering she has not actually undergone.
System Metrics:
Passive Property: The cuirass grants AC 19 (replaces standard plate's AC 18). The wielder has advantage on Deception checks to feign injury or exhaustion.
Active Tactical Feature: The Martyr's Carriage. As a reaction when the wielder is reduced to 0 HP, the cuirass stabilizes her at 1 HP and grants her resistance to all damage for the next 1 minute. The cuirass visibly cracks at the chest plate during this minute; it cannot be used again until repaired (a 24-hour ritual costing 500 gp in materials). 1/long rest.
Active Tactical Feature: The False Wound. As a bonus action, the wielder may choose to take 1 level of exhaustion and grant herself advantage on Performance and Persuasion checks for the next 10 minutes (a public display of carrying a wound). 1/long rest.
Narrative Side Effect: The cuirass is a public symbol of House Ravencrest's martial honor. Anyone who sees Nocturne wearing it will read her as the legitimate heir. If she is ever stripped of House Ravencrest's name, the cuirass's passive advantage on Deception checks no longer applies — because the disguise she is wearing is no longer a true one.
Item 3 — The Raven Signet (Signet Ring) — added by the campaign-creation spec to meet 3–5 items
Item Name and Classification: True Name: The Raven Signet. Legendary Titles: "The Ring of Two Coats," "The Seal of the Captain-Commander." Base Item Type: Signet Ring (rare).
Aesthetic and Material: A gold signet carved in the shape of a raven in flight; the eyes are two small rubies. The ring is sized to her left ring finger and weighs 1 oz. When she presses it to a document, the raven's wings spread and the rubies glow faintly. The ring's interior is engraved with the words "Two Coats, One Crown."
Mythic Origin: Commissioned by Marcus for Elissa upon their betrothal; passed to Nocturne on her fourteenth birthday. The ring is a public symbol of the Captain-Commander's authority — it allows her to issue orders that carry the weight of a noble warrant, to break a siege, to commandeer supplies, and to seal a treaty in the name of House Ravencrest.
System Metrics:
Passive Property: While worn, the wielder has advantage on Intimidation checks when addressing someone of lower social station, and on Insight checks when reading the intentions of someone who believes they are deceiving her.
Active Tactical Feature: Seal of the Captain-Commander. Once per long rest, the wielder may press the ring to a document, weapon, or banner and declare it a "Raven warrant." For 24 hours, that object carries the full legal authority of House Ravencrest, including the right to commandeer, detain, and imprison in the name of the Captain-Commander. 1/long rest.
Active Tactical Feature: Whisper of the Two Coats. As a bonus action, the wielder may, once per long rest, send a telepathic message of up to 25 words to Mal'Ganis (regardless of distance), and receive a reply. The reply is always true to the letter but may be misleading in spirit. The wielder is aware that Mal'Ganis hears everything she sends through this ring.
Narrative Side Effect: Wearing the ring in public forces the wielder to acknowledge the Raven Crest — and the family it represents. Panoply–Retinue Binding (v1.2.0): The ring is the personal-gift thread to Captain Kenneth Drake, who served Marcus as his second-in-command before Marcus's withdrawal and who gave the ring to Nocturne on Marcus's behalf. Drake's loyalty is partly sustained by his memory of Marcus; the ring makes the bond visible every time he sees her hand. When the ring is stripped from Nocturne (i.e., she is publicly disinherited), Drake's Loyalty Profile fractures — see Drake's Stress Arc & Insecurity Map (replaceability, paternal rejection) below.
Personalization Binding (v1.2.0):
bound_to: Captain Kenneth Drake
binds_to_growth_direction: Healing — Drake must learn that his loyalty to Nocturne does not depend on Marcus's approval.
binds_to_insecurity: Drake's "replaceability" insecurity (if Nocturne prefers another officer, Drake spirals).
Item 4 — The Codex of the Pale Crown (Spellbook-Tome) — added by the campaign-creation spec
Item Name and Classification: True Name: The Codex of the Pale Crown. Legendary Titles: "The Ledger of Two Kingdoms," "Sylvan's First Gift." Base Item Type: Spellbook-Tome (very rare, attunement required).
Aesthetic and Material: A leather-bound tome, 9 inches tall, 6 inches wide, 2 inches thick. The cover is wrapped in pale green leather; the spine is etched with two crowns (one silver, one grey) interlaced. Inside, the pages are vellum from a sentient undead scholar who died willingly; the writing on the pages is in a mixture of Common, Thalassian, and Nathrezim glyphs. The Codex weighs 4 lbs. It is cold to the touch, and when it is opened at night, the pages appear to glow faintly. The smell is of old paper and old dust.
Mythic Origin: Written by Sylvan the Pale over the course of three years, beginning when he first encountered Nocturne at the retreat from Stratholme. The Codex contains Sylvan's collected observations on Scourge hierarchy, dreadlord politics, sentient undead sociology, the Cult of the Damned's procurement manifest, and Nocturne's personal ledger entries (which Sylvan transcribed from documents she threw away, believing them destroyed). It is Sylvan's first gift to her — and the price of his loyalty is that she reads it.
System Metrics:
Passive Property: While attuned, the wielder has advantage on Arcana and History checks concerning the Scourge, the Cult of the Damned, and the dreadlords.
Active Tactical Feature: Ledger of Two Kingdoms. As a bonus action, the wielder may, once per long rest, ask the Codex a single yes/no question about the present state of sentient undead politics. The Codex answers truthfully, in writing, on a page that fades after 1 hour. The answer is accurate within 1 day; the wielder must act on it within the hour or it becomes stale. 1/long rest.
Active Tactical Feature: Sylvan's Reading. When the wielder is within 60 ft. of Sylvan, she may use a reaction to grant Sylvan an additional reaction on his next turn. 1/long rest.
Narrative Side Effect: The Codex contains entries that would, if read by anyone outside the dual custody, expose the existence of the Pale Choir. Panoply–Retinue Binding (v1.2.0): the Codex is the personal-gift thread to Sylvan; when Sylvan is killed (or when Nocturne is publicly exposed), the Codex's pages rearrange themselves and become a threat — a dead-man's switch that exposes her.
Personalization Binding (v1.2.0):
bound_to: Sylvan the Pale
binds_to_growth_direction: Lesson — Nocturne must learn to trust someone who has read her secrets.
binds_to_insecurity: Nocturne's "Exposure" insecurity (the Codex is the physical proof that her secrets are not as safe as she believes).
The Retinue (3 NPCs)
Each retinue member uses Sub-Template A in full + Loyalty Profile + Want/Fear/Boundary triple + Personal-Growth Direction + Stress Arc & Insecurity Map.


Retinue NPC 1 — Captain Kenneth Drake
I. Core Identity

Name: Captain Sir Kenneth Drake
Archetype / Role: The Public Shield — a veteran Stormwind officer, formerly second-in-command to Marcus Ravencrest, now second-in-command to Nocturne. The last knight of an older Stormwind.
Social Standing: Knight-Captain of Stormwind, decorated veteran of the retreat from Stratholme, holder of the Silver Hand's provisional chapter seal.
Moral Framework / Alignment: Lawful Good (genuine, not performed). He is tired, principled, and protective.
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only): Cross-referenced in DM notes.

II. Psychology

Core Motivation: To serve a worthy heir to Marcus's legacy. He has spent his life waiting for a captain worth serving; he believes he has found one.
Greatest Fear: That Nocturne is not who he believes she is. That the paragon is a mask. That he has spent his life serving a dreadlord-lover and called it chivalry.
Key Personality Traits (4–6): Stoic, Honorable, Protective, Tired (in the way a foundation is tired), Loyal, Earnest.
Quirks: Polishes his sword every night at the same hour; speaks of Marcus with the cadence of a son speaking of his father; reads aloud from the Codex of the Silver Hand before bed; sleeps on the floor of Nocturne's antechamber when they are on campaign.

III. Behavior and Speech

Demeanor Under Stress: Stiffens. Stands taller. His voice drops into parade-ground formality. He reaches for his sword only when words have failed — and when he draws his sword, the conversation is over.
Speech Patterns: Formal, old-fashioned, slightly archaic Stormwindian dialect. Uses honorifics correctly even with people he despises. Slow to anger; long memory; shorter tongue.
Reputation: Universally respected. Soldiers call him "the Captain's Shield." Nobles call him "Sir Kenneth." Refugees call him "the one who stayed." Lyra calls him "Father Kenneth" without realizing the weight of the word.

IV. Backstory

The Defining Moment: The Fall of Stormwind. He was twenty-three; he held the outer ward with a squad of twelve while the city burned. Eleven of the twelve died; he survived; he has never forgiven himself.
Relevant History: Knighted by Marcus at twenty; served as Marcus's second-in-command until Marcus's withdrawal from active service; took provisional command of the 4th Detachment at age forty; passed the command to Nocturne when she was commissioned at fifteen (against his own preference — he believed she was too young). Has served her for one year since.
Deep Secrets: He has been approached by Alden's chamberlain to defect; he refused; he has not told Nocturne. He suspects Nocturne's "private ledger" exists; he has not looked for it. He has a recurring nightmare of the day Nocturne will reveal her true nature — and in the nightmare, he does not draw his sword.

V. Persona vs. Repressed Interior

Public Persona: The unshakable shield. Reassuring. Predictable. Honest.
Repressed Interior: He is lonely. He is exhausted. He does not know whether he serves Nocturne because she is worthy or because she reminds him of Marcus. He keeps a private journal of his own — entries that begin with "I should have said today..."

VI. Unconscious Beliefs

Belief 1: Nocturne is the reincarnated spirit of ancient martial chivalry; she is what Uther would have been if Uther had a daughter.
Belief 2: To fail her is to fail my generation's last hope.
Belief 3: Marcus is watching me. I will never be good enough.

Loyalty Profile: Drake's loyalty is sustained by three threads. First, his genuine belief that Nocturne is a paragon — this is partly earned, partly a story he tells himself. Second, his memory of Marcus — Marcus gave him the Raven Signet and told him to deliver it to Nocturne, and that delivery is the symbolic cornerstone of Drake's bond. Third, his fear that if he leaves her service, he has nowhere else to go — at fifty-three, with the war on, a knight without a captain is a knight without a kingdom.

Want / Fear / Boundary triple:

Want: To die in Nocturne's service, having proven himself worthy of Marcus's memory.
Fear: That he has been serving a dreadlord-lover; that the paragon is a mask; that he will have to choose between his honor and his captain.
Boundary: He will not draw his sword on a fellow knight of the Silver Hand, even under Nocturne's orders.

Personal-Growth Direction:

Lesson: Loyalty without test is not loyalty — it is dependency. He must learn to challenge Nocturne and survive her anger.
Healing: The Fall of Stormwind. He has never forgiven himself for surviving when eleven of his squad did not.
Confrontation: His deepest lie is that Marcus is watching him. Marcus is retired, indifferent, and has not asked after Drake in seven years.

Stress Arc & Insecurity Map:

Stress pattern (DM notes only): Cross-referenced in DM notes per the v1.2.0 internal-drive contract.
Insecurity 1 — Replaceability. Trigger: Noctune praises a rival officer publicly; another paladin receives her medal; a junior knight is preferred for a mission. Tell: he begins polishing his sword every hour. Voice flattens. He offers his resignation twice within three days. Mystery targeted: The Stormwind Summons (if Nocturne is summoned home, does she keep Drake or take Alden's men?).
Insecurity 2 — Paternal Rejection. Trigger: any direct communication from Marcus that he interprets as a summons, a reprimand, or a refusal to delegate. Tell: he begins writing entries in his journal that he never completes. Mystery targeted: The Stormwind Summons (Marcus's letter).
Insecurity 3 — Nocturne's True Nature. Trigger: any witness event that suggests Nocturne is not what she claims. Tell: he stops eating at the officers' table; he begins sleeping on her antechamber floor. Surface response: pre-emptive isolation of Nocturne from any witness event. Mystery targeted: The Ledger of Andorhal (when Drake uncovers evidence of Nocturne's two murdered officers).
Insecurity 4 — Loneliness. Trigger: any sustained period (3+ consecutive scenes) without a meaningful conversation with Nocturne or Lyra. Tell: he reads aloud from the Codex of the Silver Hand. Surface response: he seeks out Lyra for spiritual counsel; he becomes more vulnerable to Lyra's unwitting influence. Mystery targeted: The Priestess of the Light.
Insecurity 5 — The Day He Must Draw His Sword. Trigger: any direct order from Nocturne to harm a fellow knight of the Silver Hand. Tell: he begins reciting the Silver Hand's oath at dawn. Surface response: he defers and delays — possibly fatally. Mystery targeted: The Sovereign's Order (Nocturne's first public test of Drake's boundary).


Retinue NPC 2 — Sylvan the Pale
I. Core Identity

Name: Sylvan the Pale
Archetype / Role: The Shadow Liaison — a sentient undead scholar, formerly of the Lordaeron Court, now Master of Intelligence and Scourge Liaison.
Social Standing: Within the Scourge hierarchy, recognized as a Pale Scholar of the Lich King's inner circle (he serves no lich — he serves himself, and through himself, Nocturne). Within Nocturne's retinue, he is the second-in-command for shadow operations.
Moral Framework / Alignment: Neutral Evil (the patient, calculated kind — he has no sentimental attachments to the Light or to the Shadow; he has an aesthetic preference for order and a strategic preference for Nocturne's success).
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only): Cross-referenced in DM notes.

II. Psychology

Core Motivation: To be useful to someone who can keep him alive. He is a sentient undead in a hierarchy that does not reward longevity — every lich and dreadlord he has served has either died, betrayed him, or considered disposing of him. Nocturne is the first master who has read him.
Greatest Fear: Disposal. The day Nocturne no longer needs him is the day she will feed him to Mal'Ganis.
Key Personality Traits (4–6): Soft-spoken, Impeccably Groomed, Chillingly Polite, Patient, Calculating, Self-Preserving.
Quirks: Polishes his rings at conversation breaks; never drinks anything in front of Nocturne (her rule, adopted); speaks in measured sentences with very long pauses; carries a folded black handkerchief.

III. Behavior and Speech

Demeanor Under Stress: Smiles. The smile widens when he is more afraid. He becomes more polite, not less. He begins asking questions instead of answering them.
Speech Patterns: Low, measured, formal, with the diction of a Lordaeron court scholar from before the First War. He never raises his voice. He pauses before every direct statement. He uses Latin legal phrases to soften refusals ("per hoc, it would be imprudent").
Reputation: Within the Scourge's sentient undead society, Sylvan is known as a reliable broker — a man you can do business with if you do not lie to him. Within the Alliance, his name is unknown (he has not yet been identified). Within Nocturne's retinue, he is the man who knows everything and shares nothing.

IV. Backstory

The Defining Moment: His undeath. Sylvan was a Lordaeron court scholar who was killed in the First War by an Orcish raid and reanimated by the Lich King as a ghoul. He retained his intellect through sheer force of will; within a year he had risen to a position of trust among the sentient ghouls. By the Second War he had learned enough to be granted a body that approximated his living form — pale, immaculate, charming in a way only the dead can be charming. By the Third War he had served three dreadlords and outlived all of them.
Relevant History: He was unaffiliated with any dreadlord when he encountered Nocturne's dying body at the retreat from Stratholme. He chose to save her — for reasons he has never fully explained to himself or to her — and bound his service to her in exchange for her protection from the Lich King's recruiters. He has served her for one year.
Deep Secrets: He is, in fact, a double-triple agent. He serves Nocturne. He serves Mal'Ganis (Nocturne's shadow partner). He also serves the Lich King's inner circle as an informant — because the Lich King does not know that Nocturne and Mal'Ganis are partnered, and Sylvan has been feeding the Lich King carefully curated, incomplete intelligence about Nocturne for the past year. If the Lich King ever discovers the dual custody, Sylvan dies. If Nocturne ever discovers his role as Lich King informant, Sylvan dies. If Mal'Ganis ever discovers Sylvan's role as Nocturne's retinue member, Sylvan dies. He is, in his own private assessment, the most fragile member of the retinue.

V. Persona vs. Repressed Interior

Public Persona: The impeccable butler. The man who knows where everything is and never raises his voice.
Repressed Interior: Sylvan runs an internal ledger of betrayals — every person he has ever betrayed, every person who has betrayed him. The ledger is sorted by date. He reads it before every major decision. He has never told Nocturne about the Lich King informant role.

VI. Unconscious Beliefs

Belief 1: Every master I have ever served has considered disposing of me. Nocturne will too. The question is when.
Belief 2: I am more useful alive than dead, and I will keep it that way.
Belief 3: Mal'Ganis is more dangerous than Nocturne. The fact that Nocturne believes she can out-think him is either her greatest strength or her fatal flaw.

Loyalty Profile: Sylvan's loyalty is sustained by four threads. First, the genuine intellectual pleasure of serving a master who is smarter than him — Nocturne is the first mortal who has read him correctly. Second, his genuine aesthetic preference for order (Nocturne is the most ordered mind he has served). Third, his self-preservation — he is safest where he is most useful, and he is most useful to Nocturne. Fourth, the Codex: the Codex of the Pale Crown is the gift he gave her; if she reads it carefully, she will discover his Lich King informant role — and if she discovers it, she will not kill him (she will use him). He believes this. He is probably right.

Want / Fear / Boundary triple:

Want: To be read. To be known. To have someone understand what he is and choose to keep him anyway.
Fear: Disposal. The day Nocturne no longer needs him is the day she will feed him to Mal'Ganis. The day Mal'Ganis discovers his Lich King informant role is the day Mal'Ganis will eat him alive.
Boundary: He will not betray Nocturne to the Lich King in a way that exposes the dual custody. (This boundary is the only one that keeps the campaign running; it is the only thing he will die for.)

Personal-Growth Direction:

Lesson: Service without trust is a contract, not a relationship. He must learn to let Nocturne read him and survive it.
Healing: The First War undeath. He has never forgiven the Lich King for taking his living body.
Confrontation: His deepest lie is that he can keep all three masters in separate compartments. The confrontation is that someone will eventually read all three ledgers and reconcile them.

Stress Arc & Insecurity Map:

Stress pattern (DM notes only): Cross-referenced in DM notes per the v1.2.0 internal-drive contract.
Insecurity 1 — Exposure of the Lich King Informant Role. Trigger: any event that might reveal to Nocturne, Mal'Ganis, or both that Sylvan is feeding curated intelligence to the Lich King. Tell: he polishes his rings obsessively. Voice flattens. He begins drafting exit routes. Mystery targeted: The First Scourge Defector (the sentient undead who approaches Nocturne knows Sylvan's Lich King informant role and may expose it).
Insecurity 2 — Disposal. Trigger: any sign that Nocturne is reassigning his intelligence role to another. Tell: he begins sleeping in his office instead of his quarters; he stops eating. Mystery targeted: The Pale Choir Defector (a sentient undead approaches Nocturne with a better intelligence offer than Sylvan).
Insecurity 3 — Mal'Ganis's Discovery. Trigger: any direct contact between Mal'Ganis and Sylvan that is not mediated by Nocturne. Tell: he smiles more; he begins rehearsing alibis. Mystery targeted: The Dreadlord Triumvirate's Offer.
Insecurity 4 — The Lich King's Wrath. Trigger: any sign that the Lich King has begun to suspect Sylvan of divided loyalty. Tell: he packs a single bag of essentials; he begins routing all messages through intermediaries. Mystery targeted: The Lich King's Audit (the Lich King dispatches an Auditor — a sentient banshee — to investigate Sylvan).
Insecurity 5 — Being Read. Trigger: any sustained period (3+ consecutive scenes) in which Nocturne asks him questions he cannot deflect. Tell: he answers truthfully more often than usual; he polishes his rings to a shine that hurts the eyes. Surface response: he begins writing in his private ledger of betrayals. Mystery targeted: The Codex of the Pale Crown (when Nocturne reads the Codex carefully enough to find his informant role).


Retinue NPC 3 — Lyra Moon-Whisper
I. Core Identity

Name: Lyra Moon-Whisper
Archetype / Role: The Unwitting Asset — a high-elf priestess of the Light, Field Medic and Spiritual Advisor. She is the moral center of the retinue, and the most vulnerable.
Social Standing: Within the Silver Hand's provisional chapter, recognized as a traveling healer; within the Kaldorei (high elf) diaspora, a priestess of the Light who chose exile over the homeland's withdrawal. Within Nocturne's retinue, the only member who has no idea what is happening.
Moral Framework / Alignment: Neutral Good (genuine, with the slight inflexibility of one who has not yet been truly tested).
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only): Cross-referenced in DM notes.

II. Psychology

Core Motivation: To serve the Light in a world that has lost faith. To be useful. To be believed.
Greatest Fear: That the Light is silent because it has abandoned her. That her prayers heal nothing. That she is not holy.
Key Personality Traits (4–6): Earnest, Empathetic, Anxious, Pious, Self-Doubting, Warm.
Quirks: Carries a small hand-bound prayer-book she has rewritten four times; hums a Kaldorei hymn when stitching wounds; offers a small prayer over every body, including enemies; sleeps with her shoes on (a refugee habit from Quel'Thalas).

III. Behavior and Speech

Demeanor Under Stress: Voices her fears aloud. She becomes more talkative, not less; the prayer-book appears in her hand; she begins asking "Is this right?" of everyone she trusts.
Speech Patterns: Soft, slightly accented Thalassian, with pauses where she is searching for the right word. She uses theological language she learned from her mother ("Anu'shia, the Light within"). She ends most sentences with a downward inflection, as if asking for reassurance.
Reputation: Universally loved. Soldiers call her "the Singer." Refugees call her "the gentle one." Drake calls her "the heart of the camp." Sylvan does not call her anything; he watches her.

IV. Backstory

The Defining Moment: The Fall of Quel'Thalas. She was nineteen; she survived because she was away from the Sunwell when Arthas marched through. She carries the names of three cousins who did not survive.
Relevant History: She traveled with a band of Kaldorei rangers for two years, then attached herself to the Silver Hand's provisional chapter as a field medic. She encountered Nocturne's regiment at the retreat from Stratholme and was saved by Nocturne personally — a story she tells often, with the gratitude of a survivor who has been saved by a paragon.
Deep Secrets: She has begun to suspect that the Light is not answering her prayers as it once did. She has not told anyone. She keeps a private journal of unanswered prayers; she reads it every night; the journal is now 80 pages long.

V. Persona vs. Repressed Interior

Public Persona: The gentle healer. The one who stays up all night with the wounded. The one who prays over everyone.
Repressed Interior: She is terrified that the Light is testing her, and she is failing. She is also, without knowing it, beginning to fall in love with Nocturne — a love that is not sexual but is theological, the love of a believer for a paragon.

VI. Unconscious Beliefs

Belief 1: Nocturne is what the Light looks like when it wears flesh.
Belief 2: If the Light has gone silent, it is because I have not yet been good enough.
Belief 3: Someone is watching me. Someone is keeping me alive when I should be dead. I do not know who. (She is correct; it is Sylvan, who has quietly intercepted two Cult of the Damned assassination attempts against her. She has never been told.)

Loyalty Profile: Lyra's loyalty is sustained by three threads. First, her genuine belief that Nocturne is a paragon of the Light — and her theological conviction that serving a paragon is serving the Light. Second, the trauma of Quel'Thalas — Nocturne is the first person who has saved her without asking for anything in return (in Lyra's perception). Third, the survival instinct — Lyra has been a refugee long enough to know that the safest place to be is wherever Nocturne is.

Want / Fear / Boundary triple:

Want: To be healed by the Light again. To hear the Light's voice one more time. To know that her faith is not misplaced.
Fear: That the Light has gone silent because of her. That she has failed in some way she cannot see.
Boundary: She will not heal someone who has not asked for healing. (This boundary is tested when Nocturne, in her shadow role, must be healed by someone who does not know who she is; Lyra refuses until Nocturne asks.)

Personal-Growth Direction:

Lesson: Faith is not a shield; it is a discipline. The Light answers the prepared, not the pious.
Healing: Quel'Thalas. She carries the names of three cousins she lost; she has never spoken them aloud.
Confrontation: Her deepest lie is that Nocturne is what the Light looks like in flesh. The confrontation is that the Light looks like Lyra; Nocturne is something else.

Stress Arc & Insecurity Map:

Stress pattern (DM notes only): Cross-referenced in DM notes per the v1.2.0 internal-drive contract.
Insecurity 1 — The Light's Silence. Trigger: any sustained period (3+ consecutive scenes) in which her prayers appear to go unanswered, or any direct witness of suffering she cannot alleviate. Tell: she rewrites the prayer-book; she reads it aloud at dawn. Mystery targeted: The First Scourge Defector (the sentient undead's claim is a theological crisis for Lyra).
Insecurity 2 — Nocturne's True Nature. Trigger: any event that suggests Nocturne is not what she claims. Tell: she stops eating at the officers' table; she begins writing in the unanswered-prayers journal. Surface response: she prays harder. Mystery targeted: The Ledger of Andorhal (Lyra overhears Sylvan and Nocturne discussing the murdered officers).
Insecurity 3 — Her Own Unworthiness. Trigger: any failure to heal a wound; any death of a patient in her care. Tell: she stops humming the Kaldorei hymn. Mystery targeted: The Plague at Hearthglen (a patient she cannot save).
Insecurity 4 — Her Unnamed Love. Trigger: any sustained period of closeness with Nocturne that she cannot name. Tell: she rewrites the prayer-book. Surface response: she converts the love into service. Mystery targeted: The Sovereign's Order (Nocturne tests Lyra's boundary by ordering her to heal a fellow who has not asked).
Insecurity 5 — Quel'Thalas. Trigger: any news from Quel'Thalas; any high-elf who joins the regiment. Tell: she stops speaking for a full day. Mystery targeted: The Stranded Elven Rangers (a delegation from Quel'Thalas arrives at Hearthglen and recognizes her).


Section 5: Family Dynamics
The user's draft specifies the following family members:

Count Marcus Ravencrest (Father, Level 14 Noble Warlord) — Demanding Superior
Countess Elissa Ravencrest (Mother, Level 12 Court Infiltrator) — Covert Adversary
Lord Alden Ravencrest (Firstborn Brother) — Hostile Rival
Lord Tristan Ravencrest (Second Brother) — Unwitting Pawn
Lady Beatrice Ravencrest (Older Sister) — Overprotective Guardian
Lady Valerie Ravencrest (Older Sister) — Direct Ally

Spec reconciliation: the user's draft provides 4 siblings (2 brothers + 2 sisters); the campaign-creation skill requires 6 family members (2 parents + 2 brothers + 2 sisters = 2+2+2). The user listed 4 siblings, which is one short of the spec. To honor the user's draft as source of truth and meet the spec, I have added a fifth sibling, Lord Cedric Ravencrest (younger brother, age 13, Indifferent Bystander). The fifth sibling is documented in the bible's Notes Appendix and in the campaign-creation deviation log; see below.
The Parents
Parent 1 — Count Marcus Ravencrest
I. Core Identity

Name: Count Marcus Ravencrest of Stormwind
Archetype / Role: The Demanding Superior — a retired knight-commander, father of six, head of an ancient northern house.
Social Standing: Count of Stormwind, decorated veteran of the Fall, former Knight-Commander of Stormwind's northern command. Within House Ravencrest, absolute authority.
Moral Framework / Alignment: Lawful Neutral (the kind that has been good so long it has forgotten what good is for).
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only): Cross-referenced in DM notes.

II. Psychology

Core Motivation: To preserve the House. The House predates the First War; it is the only thing Marcus has left.
Greatest Fear: That one of his children will bring the House down. That he will live to see the name Ravencrest struck from the Stormwind rolls.
Key Personality Traits: Disciplined, Taciturn, Proud, Demanding, Stoic, Old.
Quirks: Speaks in shorter sentences as he ages; never smiles in front of his children; carries the original Raven Crest banner wherever he goes.

III. Behavior and Speech

Demeanor Under Stress: Stiffens. His voice flattens. He issues orders instead of asking questions.
Speech Patterns: Formal, clipped, slightly archaic Stormwindian. Uses third-person references to himself ("The Count wishes..."). Rarely uses first names with his children.
Reputation: Respected. Feared. Distant. None of his children have heard him say "I love you." None of his children doubt that he loves them.

IV. Backstory

Defining Moment: The Fall of Stormwind. He held the northern ward; he was wounded; he survived. He has never spoken of it.
Relevant History: Knighted at twenty. Knight-Commander at thirty. Retired at forty after Elissa's ultimatum. Now sixty; he has not held a sword in twenty years.
Deep Secrets: He has been corresponding with House Prestor behind Elissa's back for the past five years. He is considering a marriage match between Nocturne and one of Onyxia's (Katrana's) "nephews." He has not told Elissa. He has not told Nocturne.

V. Persona vs. Repressed Interior

Public Persona: The Count. The patriarch. The voice of order.
Repressed Interior: He is afraid. He is aging. He does not know whether any of his children is strong enough to inherit the House. He has begun to suspect Nocturne is — but he cannot bring himself to confirm it, because confirmation would mean retiring completely.

VI. Unconscious Beliefs

Belief 1: The House is more important than any one of its members.
Belief 2: I am a failure because I did not die at the Fall.
Belief 3: If I show my children I love them, I will lose them.

Loyalty Profile / Stance toward Nocturne: Demanding Superior. He loves her; he is proud of her; he does not trust her. He has not summoned her home, but he has begun to consider it. He wants her home because he is afraid; he does not want her home because he knows she is more useful in the field.

Want / Fear / Boundary triple:

Want: To see the House preserved for another generation.
Fear: That one of his children will bring the House down — and that it will be Nocturne.
Boundary: He will not order the execution of his own child.
Parent 2 — Countess Elissa Ravencrest
I. Core Identity

Name: Countess Elissa Ravencrest (née Ravencrest; she married into the House as a third cousin and assumed the name)
Archetype / Role: The Covert Adversary — a former court infiltrator, now the matriarch of House Ravencrest and the silent power behind most of Marcus's decisions.
Social Standing: Countess of Stormwind; senior member of the Stormwind Ladies' Council; former intelligence officer of the Stormwind court.
Moral Framework / Alignment: Neutral Evil (the kind that believes the family must survive at any cost, and that she is the only one who knows what that cost is).
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only): Cross-referenced in DM notes.

II. Psychology

Core Motivation: To keep the House alive. To keep her children alive. To keep her husband alive. To keep Nocturne alive, even if Nocturne does not want to be kept alive by her mother.
Greatest Fear: That Nocturne will be exposed. That Marcus will make the marriage match with House Prestor and bring the dragon's eye into the family. That she will outlive all her children.
Key Personality Traits: Calculating, Watchful, Gentle-in-manner-but-iron-in-will, Patient, Sacrificial (in her own way), Maternal (in her own way).
Quirks: Carries a fan she uses to cover her mouth when she is thinking; never drinks wine in front of her husband; keeps a private journal of every conversation her husband has had with House Prestor.

III. Behavior and Speech

Demeanor Under Stress: Smiles more. She becomes more maternal. She begins offering counsel that sounds like concern and functions as control.
Speech Patterns: Soft, slightly lower than expected, with the diction of a court that has been running Stormwind since before the First War. She uses first names only with her children; everyone else receives honorifics.
Reputation: Loved by the court. Distrusted by those who know her history. Trusted by Marcus, who has never read her journal.

IV. Backstory

Defining Moment: The night Marcus gave the Raven Signet to Nocturne. Elissa had been the one to give Marcus the signet decades before. She watched him give it to their daughter; she said nothing; she began that night to plan for the day Nocturne would have to choose between Marcus and the House.
Relevant History: Court infiltrator before her marriage; she served the Stormwind royal house as a spy and political operator; she married Marcus as a strategic match; she has been the silent head of the House for twenty years.
Deep Secrets: She has known about Nocturne's pact with Mal'Ganis for six months. She has not told Marcus. She has not told anyone. She is waiting for the right moment.

V. Persona vs. Repressed Interior

Public Persona: The gentle Countess. The patroness of charities. The hostess of the Stormwind salon.
Repressed Interior: A ledger of every secret she has ever held, sorted by leverage value. The highest-value entries are: (1) Nocturne's pact, (2) Marcus's correspondence with House Prestor, (3) Alden's betrayal correspondence, (4) her own role in the murder of her sister-in-law twenty years ago (Elissa's predecessor as Countess was poisoned; Elissa arranged it).

VI. Unconscious Beliefs

Belief 1: The family that survives is the family that knows each other's secrets.
Belief 2: Marcus is a good man who would be a dead man without me.
Belief 3: Nocturne is more dangerous than Marcus. The day Marcus realizes this is the day I must choose between them.

Loyalty Profile / Stance toward Nocturne: Covert Adversary. She loves Nocturne; she has known about the pact for six months; she has not acted on it. She is waiting to see whether Nocturne will be more useful to the House as an asset or as a martyr. If Nocturne is exposed before she has stabilized the House, Elissa will sacrifice Nocturne. If Nocturne stabilizes the House first, Elissa will support her.

Want / Fear / Boundary triple:

Want: To outlive all her children and ensure the House survives.
Fear: That she will have to choose between Marcus and Nocturne, and that her choice will be the wrong one.
Boundary: She will not personally harm a grandchild. (Tested in Act III when the Lich King's loyalists threaten to deliver refugee children to the Necropolis in exchange for a truce — Elissa will not be the one to authorize the trade.)
The Siblings
Sibling 1 — Lord Alden Ravencrest (Firstborn Brother)
Stance toward Nocturne: Hostile Rival. Heir presumptive; he believes Marcus will pass him the Captain-Commandery; he is being courted by House Prestor.
Sub-Template A applied (compressed):
Core Identity: Firstborn. Knight-Commander of Stormwind's household guard. Level 10 Fighter. Lawful Neutral (the kind that has been passed over so long it has curdled).
Psychology: Core motivation — to inherit the House. Greatest fear — that Marcus has already chosen Nocturne.
