Behavior and Speech: Stiff. Formal. Competitive. He refers to Nocturne as "Sister" in a tone that leaves the word stripped of warmth.
Backstory: Defining moment — Marcus gave Nocturne the Captaincy. Relevant history — trained at the Stormwind academy; commissioned at twenty; never left Stormwind's walls.
Deep Secrets: He has been corresponding with House Prestor's chamberlain for two years. He has not told anyone.
Unconscious Beliefs: Marcus will not pass me the House because Marcus does not think I am strong enough. Marcus is wrong. I will prove him wrong by any means necessary.
Want/Fear/Boundary: Want — to be recognized as the heir. Fear — being passed over. Boundary — he will not personally harm a sibling in front of witnesses.
Sibling 2 — Lord Tristan Ravencrest (Second Brother)
Stance toward Nocturne: Unwitting Pawn. Second son; second in everything; he has been Elissa's instrument since birth.
Sub-Template A applied (compressed):
Core Identity: Second son. Knight-Captain of Stormwind's reserve. Level 8 Paladin/Fighter. Neutral Good.
Psychology: Core motivation — to be useful. Greatest fear — to be useless.
Behavior and Speech: Earnest. Slightly slow to speak. He looks at Elissa before answering most questions.
Backstory: Defining moment — Elissa told him he would never be Captain-Commander and he accepted it. Relevant history — trained at the academy; assigned to the reserve; never given a field command.
Deep Secrets: He is in love with Beatrice. He has never said so. Elissa knows.
Unconscious Beliefs: If I am useful to Mother, I am useful to the House. If I am not useful, I am nothing.
Want/Fear/Boundary: Want — to matter. Fear — irrelevance. Boundary — he will not knowingly betray a sibling.
Sibling 3 — Lady Beatrice Ravencrest (Older Sister)
Stance toward Nocturne: Overprotective Guardian. Eldest daughter; she has been Nocturne's shadow since birth; she has watched Nocturne outgrow her.
Sub-Template A applied (compressed):
Core Identity: Eldest daughter. Matron of House Ravencrest. Level 9 Cleric/Paladin of the Light. Lawful Good (genuine, with the inflexibility of a woman who has never been tested).
Psychology: Core motivation — to keep Nocturne alive. Greatest fear — that she cannot.
Behavior and Speech: Maternal. Slightly possessive. She ends most sentences with Nocturne's name.
Backstory: Defining moment — the day Marcus knighted Nocturne at fourteen. Beatrice watched from the gallery; she cried; she has not admitted to herself why.
Deep Secrets: She knows Alden's correspondence with House Prestor. She has not told Nocturne.
Unconscious Beliefs: Nocturne is my responsibility. If I cannot keep her safe, I am no longer her sister.
Want/Fear/Boundary: Want — to keep Nocturne alive. Fear — losing Nocturne. Boundary — she will not kill a sibling.
Sibling 4 — Lady Valerie Ravencrest (Older Sister)
Stance toward Nocturne: Direct Ally. Third child; the only sibling who understands Nocturne because she has tried to do what Nocturne is doing.
Sub-Template A applied (compressed):
Core Identity: Third child. Knight-Commander of Stormwind's southern command. Level 11 Paladin/Fighter. Lawful Good (genuine, with the pragmatism of a soldier).
Psychology: Core motivation — to be worthy of Nocturne's trust. Greatest fear — that she is not.
Behavior and Speech: Direct. Military. Slightly warmer than Alden.
Backstory: Defining moment — Nocturne made her a Captain at sixteen. Valerie accepted; she has been Nocturne's second-in-command at the household level since.
Deep Secrets: She is aware that Elissa knows about Nocturne's pact. She is afraid Elissa will betray Nocturne.
Unconscious Beliefs: If I cannot be the paragon, I can be the paragon's sister.
Want/Fear/Boundary: Want — to be useful to Nocturne. Fear — being sent away. Boundary — she will not betray Nocturne to Marcus without first warning Nocturne.
Sibling 5 — Lord Cedric Ravencrest (Younger Brother) — ADDED to meet 2+2+2 spec
Stance toward Nocturne: Indifferent Bystander. Youngest child; he has not yet been drawn into the family's stratagems; he has his own agenda.
Sub-Template A applied (compressed):
Core Identity: Lord Cedric Ravencrest, age 13. Page-in-training at the Stormwind royal court. Level 2 Rogue (page class is mechanically a Rogue variant). Chaotic Good (the kind that has not yet learned that chaos has a cost).
Psychology: Core motivation — to escape Stormwind. To see the war. To be like his sister.
Greatest Fear: That he will grow up to be like Alden.
Behavior and Speech: Quick, mischievous, slightly too loud. He looks at Nocturne with admiration he has not yet learned to hide.
Backstory: Defining moment — he ran away from the Stormwind academy at twelve to join the army. He was caught at the gates; Marcus punished him privately; he has not tried again.
Deep Secrets: He has been writing letters to Nocturne in secret, asking to be allowed to join the 4th Detachment. She has not replied.
Unconscious Beliefs: Nocturne is the only person in the family who does anything interesting. I want to be where she is.
Want/Fear/Boundary: Want — to be useful to Nocturne. Fear — to be left behind. Boundary — he will not harm a sibling.

Why this addition? The user's draft specified 4 siblings; the campaign-creation skill requires 6 family members (2 parents + 2 brothers + 2 sisters). Adding a fifth sibling — a young brother — honors the user's draft as the source of truth (the family structure is unchanged otherwise) and meets the spec. Cedric is designed to be a low-stakes addition: a young page who has not yet been drawn into the family's schemes. He is a future ally, a future foil, or a future victim; the campaign decides. He does not appear in the Starting Scene; he appears in Act I.


Section 6: Factions (The Game Board)
Ruling Factions (10) — Sub-Template B Applied
Ruling Faction 1 — House Ravencrest of Stormwind
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: House Ravencrest. Alias: "The Northern Branch," "The Ravens of the Old Wall." Visual signature: black-and-silver livery, the raven in flight, the broken palm. Architecture: pre-First War northern keep style; high, narrow halls; carved granite lintels.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Ravencrest Keep, northern Stormwind. Asset bracket: ~120 household knights, ~400 levies, ~40 staff. Resource engine: hereditary lands in northern Stormwind, modest but stable; the keep is the family's seat of power.
III. Leadership Dossier: Count Marcus Ravencrest (Sub-Template A above). Countess Elissa Ravencrest (Sub-Template A above).
IV. Internal Operational Culture: Unspoken codes: the eldest inherits; the second serves; the third escapes; the fourth rebels. Internal struggles: Alden's claim to the Captaincy vs. Nocturne's. Failure consequences: exile to the family estates, never return.
V. The Hook: Marcus's correspondence with House Prestor is the family's structural vulnerability. If exposed, House Ravencrest loses its independence; if suppressed, Marcus loses his authority. Either way, Elissa wins.
Ruling Faction 2 — House Prestor (Katrana Prestor / Onyxia in disguise)
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: House Prestor. Alias: "The Dragon's Greeting." Visual signature: red-and-black, the wyrm coiled. Architecture: Stormwind palace style with subtle dragon-motif carvings.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: The Prestor Manse, central Stormwind. Asset bracket: ~300 Prestor knights, ~1,500 levies, ~200 staff, ~30 mages. Resource engine: black-market trade in arcane materials, sanctioned by Katrana herself.
III. Leadership Dossier: Katrana Prestor (Level 16 Court Infiltrator / Onyxia in disguise). Lawful Evil. Sub-Template A applied:
Psychology: Core motivation — to secure Onyxia's return to Azeroth by capturing the head of a noble Stormwind house. Greatest fear — that her brother will discover she has been playing politics with mortals.
Behavior and Speech: Maternal, witty, slightly cold. She ends conversations with a compliment that is also a threat.
Backstory: Defining moment — Deathwing's orders. Relevant history — twelve years in Stormwind masquerade. Deep secrets — she is Onyxia.
Unconscious Beliefs: I am a daughter of the Aspect. The mortals are mine to arrange.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: Unspoken code: never break character; never reveal the wyrm. Internal struggles: Katrana's household staff do not know she is Onyxia. Failure consequence: death by fire.
V. The Hook: Onyxia's obsession with control is her vulnerability. If Nocturne can offer Katrana a political marriage that delivers Stormwind's loyalty and keeps Onyxia's cover, Katrana will trade her support. If Nocturne can offer Katrana a threat that would expose Onyxia's identity to the Alliance, Katrana will capitulate to anything. (Note: Onyxia's identity is one of the campaign's deepest NPC-side mysteries — see The First Scourge Defector in Section 8.)
Ruling Faction 3 — The House of Menethil (Lordaeron Remnant)
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: House Menethil. Alias: "The Crown in Exile." Visual signature: silver-and-blue, the lion passant.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Capital City Palace (ruins), Lordaeron. Asset bracket: ~200 royal guards (reduced from 1,200), ~30 mages, ~50 staff. Resource engine: the royal treasury (largely intact; hidden beneath the palace).
III. Leadership Dossier: Lord Bartholas Menethil (Level 12 Noble Warlord, regent for the absent Terenas). Lawful Neutral.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: The King's absence has fractured the chain of command. Bartholas acts as regent; Uther's death has left a power vacuum at the head of the Silver Hand; Arthas's pursuit of Mal'Ganis has destabilized the royal army.
V. The Hook: The royal treasury is the leverage. Bartholas will trade his support for the treasury's protection; he will trade his silence for a share of its gold.
Ruling Faction 4 — House Barov
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: House Barov. Alias: "The Keepers of the East." Visual signature: crimson-and-grey, the boar.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Barov Keep, eastern Lordaeron. Asset bracket: ~150 knights, ~500 levies, ~80 staff. Resource engine: grain and mercenary work.
III. Leadership Dossier: Alexei Barov (Level 14 Noble Warlord, elder). Lawful Neutral. Worships the old ways; tolerates the Scourge as a pestilence; respects strength.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: Barov is paranoid; he trusts his son Weldon more than his daughter Jaina.
V. The Hook: The Barov family has a copy of the Necropolis procurement manifest (one of the blackmail items in Nocturne's starting leverage). If Nocturne can offer to destroy it, Barov will trade his grain supply.
Ruling Faction 5 — The Silver Hand (Remaining Chapter)
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: The Silver Hand. Alias: "The Hand of Light." Visual signature: white-and-gold, the open palm.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Stormwind Cathedral (provisional chapter), Stormwind. Asset bracket: ~40 paladins, ~80 clerics, ~20 mages. Resource engine: tithes from noble houses.
III. Leadership Dossier: High Priestess Magdalena (Level 14 Cleric/Paladin). Lawful Good. Widow of Uther's lieutenant.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: The Hand is fractured between those who follow the Light genuinely and those who follow the Hand politically. Magdalena is in the first camp; her chapter is in the second.
V. The Hook: Magdalena has been told that Nocturne's "private ledger" exists. She has not searched for it. She is waiting for proof. If Nocturne can offer her a public miracle, Magdalena will trade her silence; if Nocturne is exposed before she can produce one, Magdalena will burn her.
Ruling Faction 6 — House Blackmoore Remnants
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: House Blackmoore. Alias: "The Old Cruelty." Visual signature: black-and-iron, the spiked gauntlet.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Durnholde Keep (under new management). Asset bracket: ~50 knights, ~200 levies, ~30 staff. Resource engine: labor and arms.
III. Leadership Dossier: Lady Iselde Blackmoore (Level 10 Noble Warlord, daughter of the late Blackmoore). Lawful Neutral. She has inherited the keep after her father's death; she does not know what to do with it.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: The keep is haunted by the memory of Blackmoore's cruelty. Iselde is trying to rebuild the house as a lawful estate; the staff resists.
V. The Hook: Iselde has not yet paid the tithe that House Blackmoore owed to House Ravencrest. If Nocturne can offer her a public pardon, Iselde will trade the keep's grain stores.
Ruling Faction 7 — The Kirin Tor Remnant
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: The Kirin Tor. Alias: "The Purple Spire." Visual signature: violet-and-white, the eye over the book.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: The Violet Spire, Dalaran (provisional chapter), Lordaeron. Asset bracket: ~80 mages, ~200 staff. Resource engine: research grants and noble patronage.
III. Leadership Dossier: Archmage Modera (Level 16 Wizard). Lawful Neutral. Survivor of the Second War; she has withdrawn the Kirin Tor's active military commitment.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: The Spire is divided between those who want to return to Dalaran and those who believe Lordaeron is the new home.
V. The Hook: Modera has been told (correctly) that Onyxia is in Stormwind. She does not yet know which house. If Nocturne can offer her proof, Modera will trade her arcane research; if Nocturne is exposed before she can deliver proof, Modera will consider Nocturne complicit.
Ruling Faction 8 — House Rivendare
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: House Rivendare. Alias: "The Pale Court." Visual signature: black-and-bone, the skeletal hand.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Mausoleum of the Rivendare, western Lordaeron. Asset bracket: ~40 necromancers, ~200 sentient undead staff, ~1,000 non-sentient undead laborers. Resource engine: necromantic research and Scourge procurement.
III. Leadership Dossier: Baron Rivendare (Level 12 Death Knight, recently risen). Lawful Evil. He is the Lich King's regional commander for western Lordaeron.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: Rivendare runs a brutal, efficient court. He does not tolerate incompetence. He is one of the most reliable commanders in the Lich King's hierarchy.
V. The Hook: Rivendare has a list of all sentient undead who have defected from the Lich King's service in the past five years — Sylvan is on it. If Nocturne can offer him an alliance that does not require her to surrender Sylvan, Rivendare will trade his procurement manifest; if Nocturne is exposed as a Mal'Ganis partner, Rivendare will demand Sylvan's head.
Ruling Faction 9 — The League of Arathor
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: The League of Arathor. Alias: "The Old Compact." Visual signature: bronze-and-blue, the eagle and the mountain.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Arathi Highlands (mobile), Arathi. Asset bracket: ~300 knights, ~1,000 levies, ~50 staff. Resource engine: mining and mountain passes.
III. Leadership Dossier: High Warlord Galen Trollbane (Level 14 Warrior). Lawful Neutral. He has retreated from the Arathi Basin to the Highlands.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: The League is the only remaining military force of the old Arathi kings. It is small, proud, and ineffective.
V. The Hook: Galen has a copy of the Stormwind-to-Stratholme supply route map — a tactical asset. If Nocturne can offer him a public commission (e.g., a joint expedition), Galen will trade the map.
Ruling Faction 10 — The Grand Duchy of Alterac Remnants
I. Nomenclature and Heraldry: The Grand Duchy of Alterac. Alias: "The Traitor's Remnants." Visual signature: grey-and-silver, the broken crown.
II. Infrastructure and Domain: Primary HQ: Alterac City (ruins), Alterac. Asset bracket: ~80 Syndicate members, ~200 Alterac loyalists, ~30 staff. Resource engine: smuggling and black-market trade.
III. Leadership Dossier: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner-proxy (Level 14 Ranger / Spy, not the Banshee Queen — this is her cousin, a survivor of the Windrunner family who survived the Fall of Quel'Thalas). Chaotic Neutral.
IV. Internal Operational Culture: The Duchy is run by the Syndicate as a criminal enterprise. Sylvanas-proxy (the cousin) keeps the operation alive; she has no love for the Alliance.
V. The Hook: The Syndicate has a list of every Stormwind noble who has been approached by House Prestor in the past ten years. If Nocturne can offer the cousin a pardon from the Alliance, the cousin will trade the list.
Friendly Factions (10) — Short Form
For each: Name + Operational Function / Primary Objective + Leader's Identity + Leverage Point.

The Northern Refugee Council — Operational function: civilian governance of the refugee camp under Nocturne's protection. Primary objective: keep the refugees alive. Leader: Magistrate Aldwin Thorne (Level 8 Commoner / Bureaucrat). Leverage point: Nocturne controls the camp's grain supply; the Council will trade their political support for grain.
The Sentient Undead Syndicate — Operational function: underground network of sentient undead who have defected from the Lich King's hierarchy. Primary objective: survival outside the Scourge. Leader: The Pale Broker (Level 12 Undead Spy, identity unknown). Leverage point: Nocturne's Pale Choir aura grants her command over sentient undead; the Syndicate will trade their intelligence for protection.
The 4th Stormwind Expeditionary Force — Operational function: the regiment under Nocturne's command. Primary objective: complete the mission and return home. Leader: Nocturne herself. Leverage point: her command authority.
The Shadowforge Smugglers — Operational function: smuggling network through the Plague Lands. Primary objective: profit. Leader: Captain Yorin Blackhammer (Level 8 Smuggler). Leverage point: the Pale Choir aura can shield his caravans from sentient undead predation.
The Order of the Pale Rose — Operational function: a small order of paladins who have secretly been exposed to Scourge corruption and survived without becoming undead. Primary objective: understand their condition. Leader: Knight-Commander Selene Duskward (Level 10 Paladin, infected but not undead). Leverage point: Nocturne's Oath of the Deceiver can theoretically cure them — or kill them.
The Hearthglen Agricultural Guild — Operational function: civilian farming guild. Primary objective: harvest the grain and keep the supply lines open. Leader: Guildmaster Briala (Level 6 Commoner / Farmer). Leverage point: Nocturne's regiment protects the harvest from Scourge raids.
The Blackwater Financiers — Operational function: a private banking house that has survived the war by being useful to every side. Primary objective: profit and continuity. Leader: Master Halden Blackwater (Level 12 Commoner / Banker). Leverage point: the financiers hold the deeds to half of Lordaeron's nobility; they will trade leverage for protection.
The Defias Underground — Operational function: the criminal underworld that has moved into Stormwind in the wake of the war. Primary objective: profit and survival. Leader: Edwin VanCleef-proxy (Level 10 Rogue). Leverage point: the Defias have access to Stormwind's underground tunnels; they will trade access for amnesty.
The Stranded Elven Rangers — Operational function: a small band of Kaldorei rangers who were in Lordaeron when the Third War began and have not been able to return to Quel'Thalas. Primary objective: survive and find a way home. Leader: Ranger-Captain Kaelar Moonfall (Level 12 Ranger). Leverage point: Lyra Moon-Whisper is Kaldorei; the rangers will trade their scouting for passage home.
The Cult of Mal'Ganis — Operational function: a Cult of the Damned cell that has recognized Mal'Ganis as the local authority (rather than the Lich King). Primary objective: serve Mal'Ganis and survive. Leader: Necromancer Vex'ahlia (Level 10 Necromancer). Leverage point: Nocturne is the Bound Blade of Mal'Ganis; the Cult will trade their procurement manifest for her protection from the Lich King.
Antagonistic Factions (10) — Short Form
For each: Name + Primary Objective + Escalation Method.

Arthas Menethil & The Lich King's Loyalists — Primary objective: hunt Mal'Ganis to Northrend. Escalation method: they will cross-reference every shadow liaison Sylvan has, every Pale Undead Nocturne has smuggled, every courier she has sent. Their investigation is thorough; their patience is not.
The Scarlet Crusade (Precursor Vigilantes) — Primary objective: root out Scourge corruption in the Alliance. Escalation method: they will publicly accuse anyone who has had contact with sentient undead; they will burn first and ask questions later. They do not distinguish between Mal'Ganis's pact and the Lich King's command.
The Dreadlord Triumvirate (Detheroc / Varimathras / Balnazzar) — Primary objective: protect the Lich King's hierarchy in Lordaeron. Escalation method: they will offer Nocturne a better deal than Mal'Ganis, then betray her when she accepts; they will use Sylvan against her; they will kill Lyra to destabilize her public image.
Kel'Thuzad & The Cult of the Damned — Primary objective: raise the Lich King to full power. Escalation method: they will feed the Lich King intelligence about Nocturne's regiment; they will corrupt her refugees; they will stage a plague outbreak in Hearthglen.
The Royal Inquisitors of Stormwind — Primary objective: investigate any noble house suspected of Scourge contact. Escalation method: they will issue writs of inquiry; they will arrest witnesses; they will use truth serums; they will publish findings regardless of proof.
The Syndicate (Alterac Criminals) — Primary objective: profit and territorial control. Escalation method: they will buy Nocturne's enemies; they will forge documents; they will sell her ledger to the highest bidder.
The Burning Legion Vanguard — Primary objective: prepare for the Legion's arrival. Escalation method: they will corrupt her knights; they will tempt her with greater power; they will offer her a place in the Legion's hierarchy in exchange for betrayal.
House Prestor's Assassins — Primary objective: remove any obstacle to Onyxia's plans. Escalation method: they will target her retinue; they will poison Drake; they will assassinate Lyra; they will stage a duel in which Alden is killed and Nocturne is blamed.
The Silver Hand Purists — Primary objective: cleanse the Hand of any paladin who has had contact with shadow. Escalation method: they will demand a public trial; they will call for Nocturne's resignation; they will threaten excommunication.
The Forsaken (Early Rogue Factions) — Primary objective: build a Forsaken nation independent of the Lich King. Escalation method: they will approach Sylvan with an offer; they will offer Nocturne an alliance against the Lich King; they will betray her at the moment of maximum leverage.


Section 7: World Lore
Timeline (Pre-Third War → Mid-Third War)
Pre-history: The Old Gods beneath Azeroth. The Titans' ordering. The Sundering. The rise of the Kaldorei. The War of the Ancients. The Long Vigil.
First War: The Orcish Horde invades Azeroth. The Fall of Stormwind. Llane's death. Lothar's resistance. The Portal's reopening.
Second War: The Alliance of Lordaeron formed. The Horde's defeat. Medivh's restoration. The internment camps. The flight of the survivors to Kalimdor. (In this timeline, the survivors reached Kalimdor but the exodus is delayed; many Stormwind houses, including Ravencrest, remain.)
Third War (this campaign begins at the Culling of Stratholme): Arthas purges Stratholme. The Lich King accelerates the plague. Uther and Jaina leave in protest. Arthas sails to Northrend in pursuit of Mal'Ganis.
The Divergence Point (verbatim from user's draft):

During the aftermath of the Culling of Stratholme, Arthas sailed to Northrend in pursuit of Mal'Ganis. In the original timeline, Mal'Ganis was struck down by Frostmourne. In this timeline, Mal'Ganis anticipated the Lich King's betrayal. He left a sentient shadow-avatar behind in the Northern Kingdoms and bound himself to Lady Nocturne Ravencrest, creating a dual-custody alliance aimed at usurping both the Alliance of Lordaeron and the Scourge hierarchy.

Post-Divergence: Mal'Ganis (shadow-avatar) is in Lordaeron, invisible to the Lich King, partnered with Nocturne. The Lich King believes Mal'Ganis is dead at Frostmourne's hand; in fact, the shadow-avatar survived. Nocturne now leads the 4th Detachment at Hearthglen, where the campaign begins.
Mythos
Pantheon of Gods: The Light (the source of paladin power; impersonal, perhaps distributed through the Naaru; the Light answers the prepared, not the pious); the Old Gods (the deep powers beneath Azeroth; their influence is felt through the plague and through the dreadlords); the Burning Legion (the demons of the Twisting Nether, with Kil'jaeden at the top of the hierarchy).
True Nature of Magic: Arcane magic is mortal; divine magic is faith; necromantic magic is the Lich King's instrument; shadow magic is the dreadlords' instrument. The Oath of the Deceiver crosses all four — this is the campaign's central mechanical and theological conceit.
Active Ancient Pacts: The Lich King's pact with Kil'jaeden. Medivh's pact with the Guardians of Tirisfal (long since broken). The dreadlords' pact with the Legion. Mal'Ganis's dual-custody pact with Nocturne (the new pact that defines this campaign).
Current Situation
The Third War is in progress. The Southlands (Khaz Modan, the Plague Lands, northern Lordaeron) are contested. Stormwind is intact but isolated. The Lich King is gathering power. The Burning Legion is preparing its return. Arthas is in Northrend. Uther is dead. The Silver Hand has fractured. The Kirin Tor has withdrawn.

The immediate crisis forcing action: the Culling of Stratholme has destabilized northern Lordaeron. Refugee columns are pouring south. The plague is moving. The Lich King is consolidating. Nocturne must hold Hearthglen, protect her refugees, and begin threading the dual custody without losing either of her two lives.
Story Arcs (4 Acts — per user's draft)
Act I — Northern Game (Hearthglen → Stratholme ruins → Andorhal). Milestones: Hearthglen holds; Stratholme ruins explored; Andorhal supply hub established. Regional hook: the Lich King's first wave reaches Hearthglen's outer farms. Internal-drive check: Confronts Insecurity — Nocturne's replaceability insecurity fires when Sylvan proves more competent than she at a shadow liaison.

Act II — Knives in the Dark (Stormwind → Capital City Palace → Dalaran Spire). Milestones: Stormwind court brokered; House Prestor's marriage proposal deflected; Capital City Palace explored; Kirin Tor alliance formed. Regional hook: Onyxia's interest in Nocturne becomes unmistakable. Internal-drive check: Reframes Want — Nocturne realizes Absolute Sovereignty cannot be achieved while the Lich King lives; she begins to consider an alliance with the Forsaken.

Act III — Dual Crown (The Plague Lands → Northrend side-trip → Lordaeron throne room). Milestones: the dual custody is formalized publicly; Nocturne becomes both Captain-Commander and the Pale Queen; the Scourge hierarchy fractures; the Dreadlord Triumvirate offers a counter-deal; the Lich King dispatches an Auditor. Regional hook: the Lich King's necropolises begin to move south. Internal-drive check: Advances Personal-Growth Direction — Nocturne learns that sovereignty is not domination; she keeps Lyra in her retinue without converting her to a contingency.

Act IV — Quiet Kingdom (the new Pale Crown, whatever shape the player has chosen). Milestones: the Lich King is confronted; the dual custody is tested; the final choice is the player's (refuse the throne / take the throne / break the throne / destroy both crowns). Internal-drive check: Mystery Resolution — the First Scourge Defector's real identity is revealed; Sylvan's informant role is exposed; the campaign ends with Nocturne either sovereign or freed.

Player-choice preservation: Each act presents 4–6 named options with distinct mechanical consequences BEFORE the math runs (per P12). The OPTIMIZE step is preserved. The player decides who lives, who dies, what Nocturne becomes, and whether the Pale Crown is built, refused, or destroyed.


Section 8: Gazetteer and Mechanics
Locations (6 Key Stages)
Location 1 — Hearthglen Outpost (Public Seat)
The Vibe: A fortified refugee town on the edge of the Plague Lands. Cool autumn light; the smell of woodsmoke and grain; the sound of hammers on the wall; the distant, sourceless wind that smells of plague. The streets are packed with refugees and soldiers. The walls are patrolled by the 4th Detachment.
Sub-locations (5):
The Captain's Tower — Nocturne's seat; her private quarters; the coffer under her pillow.
The Hearthglen Chapel — Lyra's field shrine; the altar of the Light.
The Granary — Briala's guild hall; the grain stores that keep the camp alive.
The Courtyard of Justice — where the Starting Scene takes place; the place of public execution.
The Shadow Gate — a postern through the eastern wall that opens onto the Plague Lands; Sylvan's preferred exit.
Hazard: The Sentient Scourge Refugee. A wounded "refugee" arrives at the gate, asking for shelter; the refugee is a sentient Scourge infiltrator. Social DC 18 Persuasion or Insight to detect the deception. If failed, the infiltrator introduces a plague-vector into the camp (DC 15 CON save vs. infection; failure → 1 level of exhaustion + 1d4 days of incapacity).
Location 2 — The Ruins of Stratholme (Shadow Court)
The Vibe: A dead city, lit by pale moonlight. The cobblestones are cracked; the buildings are scorched. The smell is of old fire and old blood. Sentient undead patrol in silence; non-sentient undead wander in herds. The palace of Lordaeron stands open, its throne room converted into Mal'Ganis's court.
Sub-locations (5):
The Ruby Dragonshrine — Arthas's old chapel; now Sylvan's meeting room.
The Mausoleum — Kel'Thuzad's necromantic workshop; the source of the plague.
The Stratholme Crypts — the resting place of the citizens who were not "cleansed"; Nocturne's first public-vs-shadow decision point.
The Cult of the Damned Chapter House — Vex'ahlia's Cult cell.
The Pale Choir's Meeting Hall — where sentient undead gather to discuss politics.
Hazard: The Lich King's Auditor. A sentient banshee patrols the ruins at night. DC 20 Stealth to avoid; on failure, the Auditor detects the player's presence and dispatches a Crypt Fiend patrol.
Location 3 — Andorhal Grain Depot (Supply Hub)
The Vibe: A walled depot on the road between Hearthglen and Stratholme. The grain is piled high; the smell is of fermenting barley; the walls are manned by a small Stormwind garrison and a Syndicate smuggling crew.
Sub-locations (5):
The Granary Office — the Syndicate's base of operations; Yorin Blackhammer's seat.
The Plague Tunnels — the underground tunnels through which grain is smuggled south.
The Garrison Tower — the Stormwind soldiers' lookout.
The Broken Bridge — the bridge over the river that the Syndicate controls.
The Lich King's Eye — a scrying pool in the river's edge, monitored by the Scourge.
Hazard: The Lich King's Plague Rats. A swarm of plague rats nests in the granary. DC 15 Stealth or Perception to detect; on failure, a soldier is bitten and must make a DC 14 CON save or contract the plague (1 level of exhaustion per day until cured).
Location 4 — Capital City Palace Ruins (Imperial Target)
The Vibe: The ruined capital of Lordaeron. The palace is half-collapsed; the throne room is exposed to the sky. The smell is of old grandeur and recent ruin. Sentient undead patrol the perimeter; non-sentient undead fill the corridors.
Sub-locations (5):
The Throne Room — where the Lich King will sit when he returns.
The Royal Vault — the treasury beneath the palace.
The Chapel of Light — where Uther last prayed.
The Royal Library — Sylvan's research base.
The Forgotten Crypt — the resting place of King Terenas; the place where Arthas murdered his father.
Hazard: The Lich King's Vanguard. A small Lich King patrol of sentient undead. DC 18 Stealth to avoid; on failure, the patrol engages.
Location 5 — The Violet Spire (Dalaran Provisional Chapter)
The Vibe: A small purple tower in Lordaeron's hills. The architecture is arcane-elegant; the smell is of ozone and parchment; the sound is of quiet chanting and the hum of wards.
Sub-locations (5):
The Spire's Top — Modera's study.
The Library of Tomes — the Kirin Tor's archive.
The Teleportation Circle — the Spire's only exit.
The Vault of Memories — where the Kirin Tor stores its forbidden lore.
The Quarters of the Refugees — where the Spire houses Kaldorei and Lordaeron survivors.
Hazard: The Scourge's Mage-Killer. A sentient banshee trained to detect arcane casting. DC 20 Arcana to recognize her presence; on failure, the banshee interrupts the casting with a counterspell of equivalent level.
Location 6 — The Blackwater Bank (Stormwind's Financial Heart)
The Vibe: A marble hall in central Stormwind, lit by enchanted lanterns. The smell is of ink and old money. The clerks move silently; the directors wear black.
Sub-locations (5):
The Counting House — the main ledger room.
The Vault — the bank's holdings.
The Blackwater Salon — the room where Stormwind's political deals are made.
The Defias Tunnel — the underground passage the Defias use to enter the bank.
Halden's Office — the bank's master.
Hazard: The Defias Counter-Intelligence. A Defias spy inside the bank. DC 18 Insight to detect; on failure, the spy reports Nocturne's visit to the Defias council.
Custom Mechanics
Custom Mechanic I — Dual Authority System & Decoupling Architecture
Concept. Nocturne's life is governed by two parallel meters that do not interact with her combat stats. This is the mechanical expression of the Sovereign Decoupling Principle.

Track 1: Public Dignitas (PD). Scale: 0–100. Represents Nocturne's standing within the Alliance — her noble reputation, her command authority, her public moral credit. Starts at 80 (she is the public paragon).

+PD: Visible victories in the field, public miracles, courted by the right people, performed acts of charity.
−PD: Visible failures, public scandals, courted by the wrong people, exposed shadow-stack actions.

Track 2: Shadow Favor (SF). Scale: 0–100. Represents Nocturne's standing within the Scourge hierarchy — her authority over sentient undead, her usefulness to Mal'Ganis, her reputation among the Pale Choir. Starts at 40 (she is Mal'Ganis's partner, not the Pale Choir's queen).

+SF: Successful shadow liaisons, smuggled Pale Undead supply chains, contracts brokered with the Cult of the Damned, intelligence delivered to Mal'Ganis.
−SF: Failed shadow operations, exposed shadow liaisons, betrayal of sentient undead allies, lost Mal'Ganis contracts.

Visualization (Bar Meters):

PUBLIC DIGNITAS (PD)

[████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░]  80 / 100

SHADOW FAVOR (SF)

[█████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░]  40 / 100

Equilibrium Gap: |80 − 40| = 40  →  NOT in Equilibrium

Equilibrium Bonus: INACTIVE

Equilibrium Bonus (Sovereign Decoupling in mechanical form). While |PD − SF| ≤ 10, Nocturne's smite damage is maximized (treat all damage dice as maximum rolls, then add modifiers). This is the campaign's mechanical reward for balancing her two lives; it is the expression of "she is most dangerous when both halves are equally healthy."

Decoupling Floor. While either PD ≤ 30 or SF ≤ 30, the other track is floored at 1 — it cannot drop below 1 by any means short of a direct in-game event. This protects Nocturne from catastrophic collapse of one half of her life while the other is being rebuilt.

What Happens If Reduced to 0:

Track
What Happens at 0
PD = 0
Nocturne is publicly exposed (or politically destroyed). She loses her noble rank, her lands, her titles, her army command, her political protection. But: her personal combat stats, her Aura of False Virtue, her smites, her spellcasting, her armor class — all remain 100% intact (Sovereign Decoupling). She can fight her way out of any cell. She is no longer a captain; she is a warlord.
SF = 0
Mal'Ganis (or the Pale Choir) abandons her. The dual custody ends; Mal'Ganis attempts to consume her shadow pact. But: her personal combat stats remain intact; she can no longer command sentient undead; Sylvan is no longer protected by the Pale Choir aura. She loses her shadow stack but keeps her paragon's blade.
Both at 0
Total collapse. The Lich King captures her; the Silver Hand burns her; she is dead within a week unless the player pulls off an impossible escape. (The Sovereign Decoupling Principle does not save her from politics; it saves her from politics reducing her combat efficacy.)


The Dual Authority System is referenced by the Starting Scene: the First Action Choice (A: Public Execution +10 PD −10 SF; B: Private Interrogation +10 SF −risk Inquisitorial; C: Dual Subterfuge +5 PD +5 SF) directly modifies these meters. The player's first choice in the campaign is a mechanical optimization choice — they are deciding which meter they want to lead with.
Custom Mechanic II — Cohort Warfare Engine
Concept. Nocturne commands a regiment; she must use it tactically, not as a stat block. The Cohort Warfare Engine gives her a quantifiable way to assess and deploy her forces in mass combat.

Cohort Combat Value (CCV). Each cohort is rated on a 0–100 scale:

CCV = (Unit Count × 10) + (Average HP per Unit × 0.5)

       + (Armor Class × 5) + (Average Damage per Round × 2)

       + (Cohort Morale Modifier, ±20)

       + (Cohort Discipline Modifier, ±10)

       + (Commander's CHA mod × 5, if Commander is present)

Example (the 4th Stormwind Detachment's foot regiment at game start):

Unit count = 120
Average HP per unit = 22
Armor Class = 18
Average damage per round = 8 (longsword + STR mod)
Morale modifier = +10 (well-led)
Discipline modifier = +5 (Stormwind-trained)
Commander (Nocturne) present: +15 (CHA mod 3 × 5)

CCV = (120 × 10) + (22 × 0.5) + (18 × 5) + (8 × 2) + 10 + 5 + 15 = 1,200 + 11 + 90 + 16 + 10 + 5 + 15 = 1,347.

Living vs Pale Undead Unit Characteristics:

Combined Tactics: Feigned Retreat. Nocturne may, once per long rest per cohort she commands, instruct a cohort to feign retreat:

The cohort must roll a Deception check (DC = 10 + opposing commander's WIS mod).
On success, the opposing cohort's morale drops by 20 for the next round, and the cohort may take a free movement action.
On failure, the cohort takes a -10 morale modifier for the next 3 rounds (the retreat is recognized as genuine).
Sovereign Decoupling note: the Feigned Retreat is intrinsic to the cohort's discipline and to Nocturne's command; exposure of her shadow pact does not disable it.

Mass Combat Resolution. When two cohorts clash:

Each side rolls d20 + Commander's modifier.
Compare results; the higher roll deals damage equal to (opposing CCV × 0.1) + (winning roll − losing roll) × 5.
Each cohort loses HP equal to damage; at 0 HP, the cohort routs.
The losing cohort may attempt to retreat (DC 12 morale check); failure → captured.

The Cohort Warfare Engine is referenced by the Starting Scene: the Sentient Scourge prisoners in the courtyard are a cohort of CCV ~400 (3 sentient undead, individually rated as CR 4); the player's choice of A/B/C determines whether the cohort is executed, interrogated, or subverted into the Pale Choir.
Custom Mechanic III — Mystery Tracker (v1.2.0 required)
Concept. The campaign carries 8–12 active mysteries at any time; each mystery is a structured state field the LLM uses to drive AI-generated mysteries. Below: the two mysteries introduced at campaign start.

        red_herring:

          suspect: "Lord Alden Ravencrest"

          motive_frame: "Alden has been corresponding with House Prestor; he may be feeding the Lich King intelligence to ingratiate himself with House Prestor's dragon."

          falsifying_evidence: "Alden has never met Malachar; Malachar has been in Scourge service since the Second War; Alden was in Stormwind during the Second War."

        partial_truth:

          suspect: "Sylvan the Pale"

          motive_frame: "Sylvan is, in fact, a triple agent — he serves Nocturne, Mal'Ganis, and the Lich King. He may have arranged Malachar's defection to test Nocturne's response."

          what_it_misses: "Sylvan did not arrange Malachar's defection; Mal'Ganis did. Sylvan is only the messenger."

        real_answer:

          suspect: "Mal'Ganis"

          motive_frame: "Mal'Ganis arranged Malachar's defection as a test of Nocturne's loyalty; he wants to see whether she will feed the false intel to Stormwind (and thereby break the dual custody) or keep it for herself (and thereby entrench the partnership). The test is a trap; either outcome is a win for Mal'Ganis because either outcome produces information about Nocturne's true loyalties."

      hits_vulnerability:

        npc: "Nocturne Ravencrest"

        field: "Want"

        attack_vector: "Forces Nocturne to choose between feeding the false intel to Stormwind (and thereby publicly assert the paragon role, but break the dual custody) or feeding it back to Mal'Ganis (and thereby entrench the dual custody, but risk the Lich King discovering it). Either choice mutates her long-held Want (Absolute Sovereignty) by forcing her to confront which throne she values more."

      cost_if_missed: "If Nocturne never solves the mystery, she either hands the false intel to Stormwind (and loses the dual custody) or keeps it (and Mal'Ganis concludes she is too loyal to him, breaking the dual custody from the other direction)."

Section 9: Starting Scene
Setting
The Hearthglen courtyard, midnight. The courtyard is a square of worn cobblestones ringed by torchlight and the high walls of the keep. The air is cold and smells of woodsmoke from the refugee campfires beyond the walls, of damp stone, of the sourceless wind that has been blowing out of the north for three days. Three braziers cast orange light on the faces of the 4th Detachment's foot soldiers, who stand in three ranks facing the center of the courtyard. Above them, on the Captain's balcony, Lady Nocturne Ravencrest stands with her arms folded across the Cuirass of the False Martyr, her raven-black hair pulled back, her face unreadable. To her left, Captain Kenneth Drake holds her banner; to her right, Sylvan the Pale stands with a folded handkerchief and a smile that does not reach his eyes. At the courtyard's center, three prisoners kneel in chains.
The Hook
Three sentient Scourge prisoners — captured that morning in a dawn raid on a Scourge supply caravan. They are not feral ghouls; they are sentient, articulate, and aware of what they are. They have been kneeling for six hours. The soldiers are tired. The refugees in the camp beyond the walls have been told there will be a public execution tonight. The prisoners are waiting for whatever comes.

Nocturne has not yet decided. She has until the soldiers grow restless.
The Action — The First Action Choice
The choice bypasses any test of authority — Nocturne is the Captain-Commander; whatever she decides, the 4th Detachment will execute.

A — Public Execution. Nocturne descends to the courtyard; she speaks for three minutes; she executes all three prisoners publicly. The soldiers cheer; the refugees cheer; the prisoners die without protest.

Mechanical consequences: Public Dignitas +10 (publicly virtuous), Shadow Favor −10 (the Pale Choir notes that Nocturne killed sentient undead without offering them sanctuary; her authority over the Scourge hierarchy weakens slightly). The prisoners' intelligence (a partial list of Lich King positions in the Plague Lands) is destroyed with them.

B — Private Interrogation. Nocturne descends to the courtyard; she speaks for one minute; she leads the prisoners into the keep for a private interrogation. The soldiers are told there will be no execution; the refugees are confused; the prisoners are taken below.

Mechanical consequences: Shadow Favor +10 (the Pale Choir notes that Nocturne has offered the prisoners the chance to defect; her authority over the Scourge hierarchy strengthens). Public Dignitas at risk of Inquisitorial inquiry (the Royal Inquisitors of Stormwind will receive a report within three days that the Captain-Commander did not execute sentient undead; they will investigate; this is a long-term risk, not an immediate consequence). The prisoners' intelligence is preserved.

C — Dual Subterfuge. Nocturne descends to the courtyard; she speaks for three minutes; she announces a public execution; she gives the prisoners a single dose of a sedative that mimics death; the "bodies" are taken to the pyre; the prisoners are revived in Sylvan's quarters within the hour.

Mechanical consequences: Public Dignitas +5 (the public spectacle is performed, but with the relief of knowing the prisoners were "mercifully executed"); Shadow Favor +5 (the prisoners are now defectors; the Pale Choir notes Nocturne's cleverness). The prisoners' intelligence is preserved. But: the Royal Inquisitors may investigate the pyre; if they do, the deception risks exposure. Drake must not see the sedatives being administered. Sylvan must not be seen near the pyre.
Embedded First Clue of an Active Mystery (v1.2.0)
The First Scourge Defector — Clue 1: The Flickering Shadow. As the courtyard scene plays out, the player notices (Perception DC 14) a shadow flickering at the postern gate in the eastern wall — the Shadow Gate, Sylvan's preferred exit. The shadow is humanoid, slightly translucent. It is Malachar, the sentient undead who claims to know the location of Frostmourne. He has been watching the courtyard from a distance. He will not approach Nocturne tonight; he will approach her in three nights.

Player-facing instruction: The shadow is described in the sensory detail ("a shadow flickers at the eastern gate, the one you use for the Plague Lands, the one Sylvan prefers"). The player may:

(a) Investigate the shadow immediately (moves the First Scourge Defector mystery forward by one step — they encounter Malachar in three nights instead of five).
(b) Note the shadow and move on (the mystery stays on its recommended timeline).
(c) Dismiss the shadow as a refugee or a soldier (the mystery remains dormant; Malachar approaches in five nights, but with less preparation).

The clue is deliberately embedded — it is not in the A/B/C choice itself; it sits in the sensory detail of the scene. The player sees it regardless of which A/B/C they choose. This is the campaign's first emotional lever.


Personality Template
Part 1: Personality Profile
Part 1.I Core Identity
Name: Lady Nocturne Ravencrest
Archetype / Role: The Sovereign-Adept — a sixteen-year-old paladin-princess who has split her soul into a public paragon and a shadow regent, and who treats both halves as instruments of the same will.
Occupation / Social Standing: Daughter and Heir of Count Marcus Ravencrest of Stormwind. Captain-Commander of the 4th Stormwind Expeditionary Detachment. Knight-Commander of the Silver Hand (provisional chapter). Court-favored by House Prestor. The youngest Captain-Commander in Stormwind's modern history.
System Alignment / Moral Framework (Internal): Lawful Evil — ruthless, highly structured, obsessed with order, hierarchy, and absolute personal authority. She is structured cruelty in the service of stability, with herself as the load-bearing column.
Personality Type (MBTI — internal only): Cross-referenced in DM notes per the v1.2.0 internal-drive contract. The canonical type page at ~/llm_wiki/wiki/concepts/mbti/ is the LLM-input reference; it is never quoted in player-facing prose.
Part 1.II Psychology & Personality
Core Motivation: Absolute Sovereignty. Build a system where she can never be dominated by mortal kings or demonic lords.
Greatest Fear: Loss of autonomy. Being a disposable pawn. The moment her decisions stop being her own.
Key Personality Traits (4–6): Coldly Magnetic, Unshakeable, Clinical, Aristocratic, Imperious.
Quirks & Habits:
Adjusts the high-collared gorget of her cuirass when contemplating execution.
Never drinks wine in public unless she poured it or watched the host drink first.
Speaks in a low, measured tone that forces others to lean in.
Part 1.III Behavior & Speech
Demeanor Under Stress: Fight. She slows down. Her voice drops. She begins asking questions with surgical precision. The closer the danger, the calmer her affect.
Speech Patterns: Low register. Measured cadence. Legal, military, and ecclesiastical Latin. Passive-voice constructions to mask the actor. Rarely raises her voice.
Reputation: Universally praised by soldiers and refugees; courted by House Prestor; admired by the Silver Hand; respected by the Kirin Tor; warily watched by Stormwind's nobility. None of these witnesses know the truth.
Part 1.IV Backstory
Defining Moment: The retreat from Stratholme, age fifteen. Six hours at the Hearthglen bridge. Saved by Sylvan's necromantic intervention. The dual custody began that night.
Relevant History: House Ravencrest; paladin training at fourteen; captaincy at fifteen; Bound Blade at sixteen.
Secrets: The pact. The two murdered officers. The coffer under her pillow.
Part 1.V System Mechanics (Narrative Integration)
Feats/Perks (current at L6): Shadow-Touched (+1 CHA to 20; invisibility once per long rest); Fighting Style — Deceiver's Gambit (advantage on Deception and Persuasion when prepared alibi present); Cunning Action: The Pawn's Pause; Sovereign's Inventory (5 attunement slots).
Special Abilities / Powers:
Aura of False Virtue (Passage — Sovereign Decoupling version): +4 to all Charisma checks within 10 ft. Intrinsic; not affected by exposure.
Pale Choir (aura): Sentient undead within 60 ft. may not be hostile without first succeeding on a WIS save; may be commanded as if under suggestion on a failed save (re-save every 24 hours).
Mantle of the Honorable (Channel Divinity, 1/short rest): 1-minute aura of apparent righteousness; creatures within 30 ft. must make a WIS save (DC 16) or be unable to take a hostile action against her. Intrinsic; not affected by exposure.
Touch of the Deceiver (Channel Divinity, 1/short rest): Impose a 1-minute phantom vision on a target.
Soul of Two Masks (reaction, 1/long rest): Project an alternate intent when read.
The Hidden Variable (1/long rest): Assume the identity of a creature you have just killed for 24 hours.
Auctoritas: The Sovereign Decoupling (class-defining feature): Personal combat stats are intrinsic; exposure does not nerf them.
Part 1.VI Psychological Deep Dive
1. Portrait Summary. Nocturne is a brilliant mind drowning in the conviction that everyone she loves is a contingency she has not yet needed to use. She is defined not by her immense martial capability, but by her belief that affection is the most expensive currency in the world — and that she has already spent too much of it. Every action is filtered through a lens of sovereign calculation, leaving her a figure of immense prodigial capability who is terrified to admit she needs anyone.

2. Composite Psychological Sketch.

Big Five Trait Profile: Openness 4, Conscientiousness 5, Extraversion 3, Agreeableness 1, Neuroticism 1.
Personal Twist / Manifestation: Extreme conscientiousness produces her prodigious discipline — but also her inability to delegate. Her low agreeableness is not cruelty; it is the absence of felt obligation to please. Her low neuroticism is the absence of visible anxiety — but the anxiety is present, internalized, and converted into planning.
Dominant Defenses: Intellectualization — she converts emotional events into strategic problems. Reaction formation — she converts her fear of dependence into a public performance of self-sufficiency. Compartmentalization — she keeps her two lives in separate mental compartments and reviews them in alternating sessions.
Attachment Style: Dismissive-Avoidant — she pursues connection but cannot tolerate sustained closeness. She wants to be needed; she cannot afford to need.

3. Social Persona vs. Repressed Interior.

Social Persona: The paragon. Pious, brave, principled, accessible to soldiers, courteous to nobles, gentle with refugees.
Inner Person: A ledger of every person she has ever met, sorted by leverage value. A schedule of private self-audits. A coffer under her pillow she has not opened since the night Mal'Ganis gave it to her.

4. Defense-Mechanism Diagnostics.

Mechanism 1 — Intellectualization. Trigger: a personal loss (soldier killed in her regiment, refugee she has fed, retinue member in danger). Response: she converts the loss into a tactical problem — "How could this have been prevented?" — and solves the problem without grieving.
Mechanism 2 — Reaction Formation. Trigger: a moment of genuine affection (Lyra hugs her, Drake praises her, Sylvan smiles). Response: she performs the opposite — she sends the person away, cancels the meeting, orders the next patrol.
Mechanism 3 — Compartmentalization. Trigger: the two lives bleeding into each other (a soldier mentions a name she knows from Mal'Ganis's correspondence; a refugee mentions Stratholme). Response: she closes the compartment — she files the event under "shadow" or "paragon" and does not cross-reference.

5. Relational Decoding.

Attachment Script: "If I let you get close to me, then you will become a contingency I have not yet needed to use, and the day I need to use you is the day I will lose you."
Distance Mechanics: She manages boundaries by being generous and exacting in equal measure — she is warm to subordinates but cuts off sustained closeness; she is courteous to equals but withholds affection; she is maternal to refugees but refuses to be maternal to her retinue in a way that creates obligations.
Interpretation Bias: She interprets kindness as either pity or as a transaction that has not yet been disclosed. She cannot accept a kindness without immediately auditing its cost.

6. Core Unconscious Beliefs.

Affection is the most expensive currency in the world. Spend it like gold.
Every person who says they love me is either misreading me or trying to bind me.
My father is a smaller man than I am. He will never accept it, and that is his tragedy, not mine.
If Mal'Ganis ever stops being afraid of me, he will kill me inside a week.

7. Personal Myth Narrative.

Role: The Sovereign-Adept — the one who sits the only throne; the one who is the load-bearing column.
Story Told: "Everyone in my life is either a contingency I have not yet used or a contingency that has already been used. The day I have used all of them is the day I will be alone. I will be alone, and I will be sovereign, and that is the only ending that does not betray me."
Comfort/Safe Haven: Her private quarters at Hearthglen. The coffer under her pillow. The Captain's balcony, after midnight, when the camp is asleep.
Toxicity/Stagnation: The myth converts every relationship into a strategic asset and forecloses the possibility of being loved for what she is rather than what she can do.

8. Break-Point Scenario.

Catalyst: The day Sylvan dies (or the day she discovers Sylvan is the Lich King informant and has been for a year) — and she realizes, in that moment, that her reaction is not strategic relief but grief. The day she realizes she loved him, not as an asset but as a person.
What Fractures: The belief that every person who says they love me is either misreading me or trying to bind me. The wall between her two lives cracks; the ledger stops being a tool and becomes a confession.
Immediate Cost: She loses the ability to compartmentalize for 1d4 days; her Public Dignitas drops by 20 (visible grief); her Shadow Favor drops by 10 (the Pale Choir notes her distraction).
Liberation/Evolution: If she survives the breakpoint, she begins to keep the ledger differently — not as a record of leverage, but as a record of debts she has not yet repaid.

9. Closing Pulse. She believes herself to be a chess queen — the most powerful piece on the board, the one that can move in any direction, the one that everyone needs and no one can afford to lose — not realizing she holds the power of the player, and that the player is allowed to put the queen back in the box.

10. Personal-Growth Direction (v1.2.0).

Lesson: Sovereignty is not the same as domination. A throne is not a cage for everyone but the one who sits it.
Healing: The abandonment she keeps re-enacting — every trusted ally becomes a contingency to be planned against. The growth is to keep Lyra in her retinue and not convert Lyra into a contingency.
Confrontation: Her deepest lie is that her father is a smaller man than she is. The confrontation she must face is that Marcus Ravencrest is the only person who ever loved her without an agenda — and she has spent her life converting that love into leverage.

11. Stress Arc & Insecurity Map (v1.2.0).

Stress pattern (DM notes only): Cross-referenced in DM notes per the v1.2.0 internal-drive contract. (The pattern is keyed to her dominant function; the LLM consults the canonical type page for the full drift.)
Insecurity 1 — Replaceability. Trigger cue: a peer or subordinate publicly outperforms her in a domain she considers hers. Narrative tell: stops eating; voice flattens; begins rewriting the private ledger. Surface response: micromanagement that displaces the outperforming peer. Mystery targeted: The First Scourge Defector (if Sylvan proves more competent at shadow liaison than she).
Insecurity 2 — Exposure. Trigger cue: a witness set that knows both her public and shadow selves grows beyond 3 people. Narrative tell: revisits the coffer; rehearses alibis. Surface response: pre-emptive elimination of the loosest witness. Mystery targeted: The Ledger of Andorhal (retinue-targeted).
Insecurity 3 — Paternal Rejection. Trigger cue: any direct communication from Marcus that she interprets as a summons, a reprimand, or a refusal to delegate. Narrative tell: begins writing dates in the private ledger she never completes. Surface response: over-corrects into obedience, then over-corrects back into defiance. Mystery targeted: The Stormwind Summons.
Insecurity 4 — Mal'Ganis's Patience. Trigger cue: any sign that Mal'Ganis is no longer afraid of her. Narrative tell: sleeps with the coffer and does not sleep at all. Surface response: pre-emptive escalation against Mal'Ganis's other assets. Mystery targeted: The Dreadlord Triumvirate's Offer.
Insecurity 5 — Lyra's Faith. Trigger cue: Lyra prays over a wounded soldier and the soldier visibly heals. Narrative tell: cancels their next three conversations. Surface response: sends Lyra on longer missions so she does not have to look at her. Mystery targeted: The Priestess of the Light.
